**`mcp-v2-understanding-2026-08.md`** (2026-08-29) explains rather than decides. MCP v2 is stateless, with state in explicit handles, server-to-client questions inverted into multi-round-trip requests, typed refusals, and consent surfaces owed to the human. It is the companion to the next file.

**`mcp-client-obligations-2026-07-28.md`** is a per-item table (A1–J3) of client duties. It marks which are library-covered, which are ours, and which are done, and rules that the sampling primitive stays un-added. It builds on #1274, #1285 and #1309. Open: Base64 sentinels, `resources/updated`, legacy -32002, enum defaults, per-request logLevel, authorization-server discovery order and issuer keying. There is a verified SDK gap on the OAuth S256 check.

**`mcp-2026-07-28-compat-matrix.md`** (undated, reflects fastmcp 4.0.0b5) pins dependencies and records the migration (`as_proxy` → `create_proxy`, `mount(prefix=)` → `namespace=`). A compatibility spike passed all four pairings, and an owner override neutralises an upstream `mcp<2` bound. Open: a live smoke runs at the P0 gate, the override is dropped when upstream catches up, and the default memory docket is single-process only.

**`mcp-client-unification-2026-08.md`** (ACTIVE; cut 2026-09-01) puts every server behind one negotiated client. Campaign 1 builds and proves the client against v1, v2 and synthetic servers; relay removal moves to campaign 2. It fixes a defect where the proxy suppressed tasks. It builds on the two docs above and #1274. Open: Apps-host revision alignment is untouched, C1-S6 acceptance and landing are pending, and the full live verification awaits owner go-ahead. One line still says b1 while later docs say b5.

**`mcp-fleet-memory-2026-07.md`** (landed S1–S5, 2026-07-15) makes MCP server memory O(1) servers for N sessions, cutting peak memory from 3.57 GB to 1.42 GB cold and 0.72 GB settled, with a budget gate in release checks. It is an earlier, separate campaign. Open: shared-process fleets for absolute-path-only namespaces are gated and not attempted.

**`hpc-mcp-runtime-semantics-1321.md`** (undated) is the umbrella handoff for #1319–#1323: one persistent `clio-kit[science]` install serving four MCP processes, external-input provenance, provider routing and local vLLM. It lists gate counts. Open: the released installer still installs legacy Kit 2.10.6 until the paired release, and the local vLLM run does not qualify AMD GPU, containers or HPC filesystems.

**`shared-mcp-runtime-integration-1319.md`** is an operator guide: one tool install serves NDP, Geo, Pandas and Plot, with no solving or building during normal discovery and upgrades done by the package manager. Open: the pin predates this contract until the paired release exists, and no HPC timings are claimed.

**`external-input-provenance-1320.md`** records `used` edges for the built-in file reader and Kit tools without opening or hashing sources, with an unknown-contract warning instead of a fabricated edge. The UI half was re-landed as presenter blocks under #1336, superseding the original UI. Open: no full-suite, live HPC or installed end-to-end qualification is claimed.

**`provider-runtime-routing-1322-1323.md`** (undated) resolves summarisation inference from the owning LM, makes `summarizer.*` configurable, and raises `LMOutputTruncatedError` on `finish_reason=length` with no repair. Open: broad matrix validation is CI-owned.

**`unified-spotter-provenance-mcp-2026-08.md`** (implemented, live-qualified August 2026) defines Spotter as a standalone read-only MCP with 15 tools. Provider selection is deployment config, there is no silent fallback, and the UI keeps a separate REST path. Open: the repo-wide tests, lint and type-check results for acceptance gate 9 are not recorded.

**`extensions-discovery-and-connection.md`** (2026-10-26) defines the journey discover → inspect → add → enable, with "installed", "configured", "signed in" and "connected" as distinct states (connected only after a real MCP handshake), four views, and a shared private-local marketplace. Open: a full installed-Desktop OAuth journey and a real Home Assistant authorization remain separate acceptance work.

**`ndp-connected-source.md`** (qualification dated Oct 18) makes NDP a connected data source with explicit Download or Link, Keycloak device-flow sign-in, scheme-routed reads and no write operations. Open: protected reads need a working Endpoint, a production realm needs its own registered client, the test directory returned no group memberships, and the public catalog's search returned HTTP 400.

**`ndp-endpoint-operations.md`** (live qualification 2026-10-18) treats Endpoints separately from catalog datasets, observes operations from `/openapi.json`, requires per-operation approval, refuses token forwarding through the service proxy, and retains responses as immutable resources. Open: a protected station-sampling call returned HTTP 401, so protected Kafka consumption is not established, and the acceptance evidence is on a private path outside the repo.

## 7. Artifacts, provenance, A2UI and feedback

**`artifacts-research-2026-07.md`** is a prior-art survey ("not a design") that lists directions: register at the output-path hook, adopt relay's `ArtifactRef`, use W&B-style versions. It cites the owner framing `b = transform(a)`, relay #58 and PR #59. It says the earlier Cowork capture design is superseded by the next file.

**`artifact-provenance-design.md`** (v2, 2026-07-16) decides that the model is never in the chain of custody, artifacts are designated rather than discovered, and the content hash is identity. Custody is tiered and attribution is lease-scoped, with a `create_artifact` tool replacing an inert field. Open: policy for agent-proposed designations, content-store budget and GC cadence, relay schema convergence timing, and whether Campaign B's container mode revives tracing.

**`artifacts-campaign-2026-07.md`** (close-out) records Campaign A as landed in slices S1–S7 (#967–#973): registry projection, `create_artifact`, version chains, transform records, content store and GC, and RO-Crate export. Path-string scrapers were deleted. Open: Campaign B, client rendering, federation transport, the replay runner and relay `ArtifactUse` convergence.

**`document-artifacts-human-review-2026-07.md`** (no date inside) makes documents format-aware views over the immutable registry, with highlight-to-comment creating an `artifact_review` part bound to version and hash. Only comments starting `@clio` instruct the agent, and a package-inventory guard blocks edits that would drop unknown parts. Open: real ONLYOFFICE/Collabora container acceptance is separate and unclaimed, and third-party extension round-trips are not guaranteed.

**`provenance-adapters-and-artifact-storage-2026-08.md`** (implemented, dated 2026-08-21, partly read) defines the ARC event highway as the parent stream, with provider-pluggable agentic provenance (JSONL, Flowcept) and artifact providers (native, CMF). CLIO owns version history and SHA-256 identity. Open: a deferred list (external CMF lineage import, remote stores, overflow policy), eleven questions for the CMF team, and an unqualified native `clio_core` store and Windows MLMD runtime.

**`a2ui-compat-campaign-2026-09.md`** (approved 2026-09-16, closed 2026-09-17) makes CLIO a truthful A2UI 0.9.1 agent and renderer, with catalogs declared in blueprints, official shapes used verbatim and durable `a2ui_action` parts. It supersedes an unexecuted Codex proposal. Open: A2UI 1.0, inline catalogs and A2A transport are unsupported, the waiting-user live cell is unobserved, intermittent Windows Core crashes are tracked on #1242, and the ledger has stale cells.

**`a2ui-release-handoff-2026-10-03.md`** is a publication handoff, not a design. It gives the combined `a2ui_fixes` branches, merge targets and release order. Open: stale version metadata, divergence counts that need refreshing, a third example blocked on missing exports, and no merge, tag or release gates run.

**`widget-visual-feedback.md`** (accepted design, expanded after the 2026-10-08 review) defines the inspect → control → render → screenshot → adjust loop, with a bounded `capture_a2ui_surface` that never returns a stale frame and saved dashboards as immutable versions. Open: VIGIL integration is deferred, no headless viewer exists, the runtime acceptance list is unmet, and the implementation is still a draft.

**`response-feedback.md`** (undated) adds Good/Bad/Remove ratings, stored in an ARC ledger with answer hash and provenance, changed only after server acknowledgement, with 409 on conflicts. Ratings do not enter prompts. No open questions are stated, and nothing consumes the ratings yet.

## 8. Sandboxing, governance and operations

**`sandboxing-campaign-2026-07.md`** (the landed record for #974) built OS write-confinement with a backend ladder, a CONNECT-only egress chokepoint and recorded `boundary.*` events, and upgraded provenance classes. It builds on #966. Open: the five live-gate results are still placeholders, and a native Windows restricted-token rung is not built. The next file supersedes its backend choice.

**`codex-sandbox-rework-2026-07.md`** replaces srt with the OpenAI Codex sandbox as the sole OS-fence backend, after srt failed to enforce on native Windows. Slices B-codex-1 to 5 are defined and srt is deleted. Open: the Network section is deferred to the next file.

**`codex-net-2026-07.md`** (owner directive 2026-07-23) de-defers the network pillar. Reads are allowed and recorded, writes are blockable and escalated, and a managed proxy chains to a clio chokepoint, proven live on Windows. Open: HTTPS CONNECT tunnels are opaque, so write detection is clean only for plain-HTTP verbs and host policy; the N1–N3 live gates are acceptance criteria not recorded as complete; Linux still needs the redirects.

**`governance-surfaces-2026-07.md`** (FINAL, acceptance record 2026-07-28) builds one governance engine on `grant_resolver`, with plan mode and hooks as data. It adds priority bands and most-restrictive-wins, deletes `chat` mode and both old hook systems, and uses an LLM-only goal judge. It builds on #1031 and #1057 and the two research docs. Open: hardening the Windows shell fence waits on an alpha external sandbox, cross-restart durability of pending defers is not wired, and one cross-repo enum needs a `declarative` entry.

**`live-gate-governance-1057-verdict.json`** records `"pass": true` with all 17 required gates true (hook fired, plan write blocked, cron fired, loop ended on a typed bound, goal met, zero degrade reasons). One non-required check, `plan_denial_in_trace`, is false, although the governance doc lists "plan write-deny + denial in trace" among the passes. Also note the verdict's timestamp (2026-07-29) differs by a day from the doc's acceptance date.

**`system-cleanup-2026-07.md`** (master plan from a nine-reviewer audit, 2026-07-01) sets ground rules such as every degradation being loud and deleting rather than gating, with phases 0–4 and an issue map. It builds on umbrellas #775 and gact-tui #237. Open: most exit-criteria boxes are unchecked, and owner-gated items remain (history rewrite, LFS quota, ratchet flip, ui-split stage 2+). The header says "Phases 2–4 open" but the execution section records Phases 3 and 4 as done, so the header is stale.

**`codex-rework-landing-2026-08.md`** (ACTIVE, approved 2026-08-25) lands four repos on develop through green-CI PRs, under rules such as no silent fallback and no ratchet raises. It runs Phases 0–6, folds in the Flowcept/CMF work and replaces the old render contract. It follows `system-cleanup-2026-07.md`. Open: non-blocking items (session-status flicker, producerless slots, inert cmf-server pipelines) and pending reviewer approvals and merges. Note "Codex" here means the agent executing a campaign, not the sandbox.

**`installation-and-storage-recovery.md`** (undated) covers older Linux hosts via a private pinned runtime (#1782), capacity recovery for conversation storage by adding file targets (#1783, needs Core 2.3.2), and a single "Update CLIO" action. Open: the screenshots do not establish the affected host's exact failure, custom topologies are not auto-enrolled, and Linux still needs host graphics, font and NSS libraries.

**`vllm-local-qualification-20260904.md`** records a CPU-only vLLM 0.28.0 run in WSL2 with a tiny Qwen model, where the Agent factory smoke returned HTTP 200 on both requests. Two failed starts are kept as negative evidence. Timings are operational evidence, not HPC performance, and the evidence JSON lives outside this folder.

## 9. Integration and release status

**`campaign-integration-landing-2026-09.md`** (LANDING; marketplace PR #59 merged 2026-09-03) records that the reviewed heads were not mergeable as-is and were fixed forward after finding five blocker classes (event-loop work, unbounded state, fabricated attribution, log-only degradations, scope holes). Seven tunables moved to config. Open: two load-flaky streaming tests, a lossy restart reshape for legacy question rows, marketplace #61 and #62, and the full suite deferred to CI.

**`beta2-integration-qualification-2026-10-03.md`** records beta-2 qualification (Agent 0.9.5b2, UI 0.11.3-beta.4): live Codex runs building linked views from a 500-row CSV, browser review, and a macOS packaging gate. Earlier failed trials are not counted as passes. Open: the third Abaqus demo lacks real exports, the original CHPC and Desktop-exit acceptance is not reproduced, session creation has no idempotency key, and the final DMG must pass the native gate.

**`beta3-integration-status.md`** (checkpoints Oct 4–5) tracks the beta-3 work: shared attention profile, connected-data adapters, model acquisition, native supervisor, marketplace Reload and Python 3.13 runtimes. The owner's Oct 5 request to publish supersedes an earlier hold, though the tail still says "Do not publish". Seven items remain outstanding, including live Google/Globus OAuth, native vLLM on a real GPU, the Delta run, a CI-red agent head and a DMG failure.

## 10. SDK subfolder: plugins, flows, fleet, memory and science

The README says to start with `megachange-plan.md`. It dates the export Oct 20, 2026, so it is stale: it omits `plugin-change-delivery`, `removal-manifest`, `model-fleet-ledger`, `science-ledger`, `acceptance-ledger` and `windows-openai-qualification`.

**`sdk/README.md`** is an index only, saying the repository copy is now the one to edit.

**`sdk/plugins-and-composition.md`** (Oct 6) decides that the plugin is the unit of distribution, trust and composition. It adopts Agent Plugins 1.0.0 plus a CLIO namespace, packs are membership only, tool-name collisions are errors and hooks run child to parent. It builds on the Sept 17 planning session. Deferred: evals in the plugin's own repo, the lesson-record schema and personal marketplace, and the optimizer gate.

**`sdk/agent-sdk.md`** (Oct 6) says plugins hold all content and agents hold only flow, identity, plugin selection and exposure. Python is the authoring surface, resolution runs at publish and at session start, and fragments carry a soft 150-token budget. It ends with "Settled in review", so no open questions.

**`sdk/plugin-change-delivery.md`** (undated) handles prompt-cache invalidation when plugins change mid-conversation, via an `apply` field with `now`, `compact` or `note`. Open: native provider paths are "next step", strict open-model templates have no cache-safe tool change, and compliance under `note` depends on the model.

**`sdk/orchestration-semantics.md`** (Oct 7) makes flows plugin content (a DSPy module with `forward(task, ctx)`), with durability as a journal in task history and code-first orchestration preferred. Eight open questions (flows as a task kind, handoff, checkpoint cap, replay of model-written code and so on) get defaults in the megachange plan.

**`sdk/remote-agents-and-protocols.md`** (Oct 6) builds peers on A2A, with Academy via an adapter and ACP as an exposure target. Open: accepted limits (no progress for long A2A jobs, local-only ACP exposure, Academy without streaming). The megachange plan puts it out of scope.

**`sdk/megachange-plan.md`** is the implementation plan. The designs are the contract, with delete-and-replace, no shims, the task layer as sole execution authority, and no silent fallback. It gives defaults for the open questions, and adds phases 6 (model fleet) and 7 (agent writes files) on Oct 23. Open: the RLM leaves wait for the `rlm` flow, and rows a cloud session cannot produce (Tauri desktop, Windows-only paths, SSH to HPC) are marked blocked. The file ends with Phase 5, which sits after 6 and 7 in file order.

**`sdk/removal-manifest.md`** lists every module removed, rewritten or kept, by AST at `2c100d5`: about 55 blueprint modules and the declared-workflow runner removed, the task layer kept, and a proposed marketplace plugin split. Its one unresolved note is that `spawn_runtime_declarations.py` did not exist at that commit. The plan and manifest disagree on whether a flow is named `plan` or `workflow`.

**`sdk/model-fleet.md`** (Oct 22) makes model choice first-class: a fleet read model, usage snapshots, explicit `model` on spawns, typed refusals instead of silent replacement, and a spending guard off by default. It builds on #1802. Eight open questions come with proposed defaults.

**`sdk/model-fleet-ledger.md`** records endpoint checks (2026-10-23), decisions M-D1 to M-D14 and acceptance rows M1–M12. M2, M3, M6 and M12 passed live. M4, M5 and M7–M10 pass in tests only, M1 is partial, and M11 waits on `rlm`. Header-capture for Anthropic and OpenAI is a follow-up (#1837).

**`sdk/long-term-memory-plan.md`** (undated) puts memory in clio-core as Markdown subject documents in six categories, with BM25 retrieval, background changes as proposals and an index capped at 2,000 tokens. Out of scope: embeddings and shared memory. It says the delegation plan was never written, which conflicts with `delegation-fork-science-plan.md` existing now, so read the memory docs as predating it.

**`sdk/memory-ledger.md`** (live run 2026-10-23) records decisions MD0–MD43 and scenarios M1–M18, all passed in what I saw, including concurrent-update conflicts and restart resume. The plan governs except where a decision row says it was wrong. M8 used a general subagent because no `explore` agent was installed.

**`sdk/delegation-fork-science-plan.md`** (base `8159955f5`; Addendum A folded in 2026-10-27, so it now governs) has seven workstreams: default delegation, self-fork, a typed science log, a Wordle study, a hidden-law study, export of flows and subagents, and publication. Hidden answers are never written to the workspace. It builds on #1825 and the ledgers. Open: a defaults table recorded in the science ledger, scenarios F1–F25 required for Done, and large exports blocked if release rights are missing.

**`sdk/delegation-fork-science-addendum-a.md`** (folded in 2026-10-27, so now a decision record) says observations cite tool calls, measurements are handed to the agent as data (`query_log`, `export_measurements`), every branch reads the whole study but writes only its own, and isolated workspaces use copy-on-write. It supersedes the plan's earlier visibility rule. Open: plugin servers that write files themselves are not confined per node (FD19), branches reading each other's claims can converge early, and F11, F13 and F15 must be re-run.

**`sdk/science-ledger.md`** is the evidence ledger for the plan and addendum: decisions FD1–FD34 and scenarios from F1. FD1, FD2, FD4, FD10–FD19, FD21–FD24 and FD29–FD34 passed, with F1–F5 passing, and FD3, FD5–FD9 and FD20 are pending. FD8 moves the showcase model to an Opus-class Claude. Known limits are FD19, FD33 (same-user `/proc` environment readable) and FD34 (live shadow not drawn). Scenario rows past F5 were not read.

**`sdk/acceptance-ledger.md`** is the evidence ledger for the megachange. It has decisions D1–D40, phase rows, live scenarios, K-numbered defects and a security review (S-1 to S-11). A row passes only with recorded evidence. Open: the Tauri, Windows-only and HPC-over-SSH rows are blocked, K-10 (fragments over the 150-token budget) is open, and S-10 (loopback privileged routes reachable by any local process) needs a decision.

**`sdk/windows-openai-qualification.md`** (run 2026-10-24/25) records an overall **fail**: the first Deep Researcher journey failed before producing a report. Defects include #1855 (repaired), and #1856 and #1857 (source repaired, live repeats pending). A 48-hour semantic qualification runs to 2026-10-27 04:50 UTC. Open: repeat live runs for #1856, #1857 and #1849, and several issues still open. Its receipts do not establish research quality, and neither full CI nor desktop release validation is claimed.

## 2. `react-loop-completion-2026-09.md`

**Date / status:** accepted 2026-09-05. Amended 2026-09-30 by the agent-loop rebuild, phase 6.

**Group:** Agent loop and context.

**Decided.** The model owns action selection in the ReAct loop, and CLIO never calls the model again after the loop returns. A response with no tool call is a normal direct response, returned as `answer` with `termination_reason="direct_response"`. A valid model-selected `submit` stays available. Parse failures and iteration-cap exhaustion stop without a forced submit.

Seven recovery mechanisms were removed: empty-tool-call retries, the post-loop forced submit, submit repair over History, schema-repair resampling, adapter tool-intent recovery, answer synthesis from observations, and empty-answer classification. The rationale given is that this is a responsibility boundary, so stronger models are not forced through recovery built for weaker ones.

**Amendment (2026-09-30).** DSPy's own `ChainOfThought` extract may run once, under these conditions:
- `agents.react_extract.enabled` is on (default true).
- The loop took more than `after_steps` model steps (default 3).
- The loop ended by `max_iters`, or by a direct response on a signature whose declared outputs were not produced.

It fills only the missing outputs and never replaces the user-visible answer. `submit`, `ask_user`/`plan_exit` yields, `context_window_exceeded`, plain `question -> answer` and short loops never extract. `enabled: false` restores the original contract.

**Builds on:** the 2026-09-05 decision supersedes the earlier landing decision recorded in `composer-pipeline-landing-2026-09.md`. The amendment cites the agent-loop rebuild doc.

**Open:** none stated.

**Supersession:** it supersedes the "ground-rule violations dropped" rationale in the composer landing doc, and it is itself narrowed by the 2026-09-30 amendment.

## 3. `model-stream-recovery.md`

**Date / status:** none stated.

**Group:** Provider and transport resilience (loop-adjacent).

**Decided.** A "connection closed mid-chunk" error proves only an interrupted transport, not its cause. The doc names gateway idle timeout, upstream failure, proxy or network disconnect as indistinguishable without gateway logs. A UI heartbeat does not keep the gateway connection alive.

DSPy retries typed transient failures only before any stream chunk is forwarded. CLIO adds narrower recovery for stateless OpenAI-compatible chat requests that propose only local function tools:
- **Before public answer text:** restart the generation. Completed tool calls are not re-executed. Interrupted reasoning stays in the transcript, closed by a service notice. Partial reasoning and incomplete tool proposals are discarded.
- **Backoff and budget:** 1s, 2s, then capped at 8s, bounded by `limits.lm_transient_retries` / `CLIO_LM_TRANSIENT_RETRIES` (default 2; 0 disables).
- **After public answer text:** report a clear provider error and keep the partial transcript, with no silent restart.
- **Out of scope:** stateful SDK engines, provider-native tools, and auth, config, policy or arbitrary tool failures keep their own paths.

**Builds on:** no earlier docs or issues are cited.

### 2. `independent-goal-controls-2026-10.md` (3,830 B)
- **Decided:** the goal controller pursues an observable objective, not an iteration counter or timer. Setting a goal starts work at once. Each completed turn gets an independent completion check, and an unmet objective continues. Explicit human limits take precedence, and omitted limits are unlimited.
  - **Judge:** it sees bounded recent evidence plus a retained progress ledger and cannot run tools. A failed judge pauses the goal, a decision needing human input parks it, and ten identical final responses stop continuation.

  - **`wait_for`** parks a goal on durable task handles. `all` waits for every task and `any` resumes after the first. `wait_tasks` stays the in-turn blocking tool.
  - **Restart recovery:** retained goals inspect task outcomes and workspace state before replanning. A pending loop wake remains, and an in-flight loop stops explicitly.
  - **Fleet:** judges for goals, variants/refinement and permission risk are chosen independently. Permission review classifies none/low/medium/high, and high or unavailable reviews escalate to the user.
- **Builds on:** it cites only external research: Magentic-One, Anthropic's long-running harness guidance and LangGraph persistence. It cites no CLIO issue numbers.

### 1. `goal-command-presentation.md` (1,408 B)
- **Decided:** `/goal` records a service notice with `source: goal` and an explicit result code (`goal_started`, `goal_stopped`, `goal_rejected`, `goal_command`). Start and stop receipts keep the objective. The conversation shows a Goal entry with a target icon and an "Open Work" action. That action only navigates; it does not re-run the command, restart work or stop a goal. Goal receipts get no "Done" footer. Older text receipts are projected from their recorded metadata, and ordinary prose mentioning `/goal` is not reclassified. The Work finder and footer use the same Goal icon, kept distinct from loops, schedules and todos, and the footer drops the duplicate todo count at narrow widths.

### 2. `independent-goal-controls-2026-10.md` (3,830 B)
- **Decided:** the goal controller pursues an observable objective, not an iteration counter or timer. Setting a goal starts work at once. Each completed turn gets an independent completion check, and an unmet objective continues. Explicit human limits take precedence, and omitted limits are unlimited.
  - **Judge:** it sees bounded recent evidence plus a retained progress ledger and cannot run tools. A failed judge pauses the goal, a decision needing human input parks it, and ten identical final responses stop continuation.
  - **Loops and schedules** are independent of goals: goal completion never cancels monitoring, and a stopped loop never stops the goal.
  - **Harness injections:** judgments, loop wakes, scheduled wakes and task completions are recorded as typed harness injections with algorithm authorship, not as human prompts.
  - **`wait_for`** parks a goal on durable task handles. `all` waits for every task and `any` resumes after the first. `wait_tasks` stays the in-turn blocking tool.
  - **Restart recovery:** retained goals inspect task outcomes and workspace state before replanning. A pending loop wake remains, and an in-flight loop stops explicitly.
  - **Fleet:** judges for goals, variants/refinement and permission risk are chosen independently. Permission review classifies none/low/medium/high, and high or unavailable reviews escalate to the user.
- **Builds on:** it cites only external research: Magentic-One, Anthropic's long-running harness guidance and LangGraph persistence. It cites no CLIO issue numbers.
- **Open:** no explicit open items. Stated limits: "completion is judged evidence, not proof of scientific correctness", and restart recovery "is not replay or rollback of arbitrary external operations".

  - Memory is Markdown subject documents in categories: profile, preferences, topics, areas, people, environments. Each fact is a line with an id and a source.
  - It lives on clio-core through `ARCStore` in the `memory` namespace, with BM25 retrieval.
  - Background changes are proposals, and the `memory_` prefix means long-term memory only.
  - Defaults: 2,000-token index cap, 30-minute idle trigger with at least 3 user messages, 60-day expiry, sensitive topics off.
- **Builds on:** `acceptance-ledger.md` D1–D29, `plugins-and-composition.md`, `agent-sdk.md`, `orchestration-semantics.md`, `docs/ARC_MEMORY_LAYER.md`, clio-core #905 (the indexer), and #771.
- **Left open:**
  - It says the delegation, fork and science plan named in an earlier draft was never written, so its F decisions do not apply. This conflicts with the existence of `delegation-fork-science-plan.md`, which uses `F` ids.
  - The blocker was that the default clio-core config did not compose the indexer, so search silently returned zero hits.
  - Out of scope: embeddings, shared or federated memory, and generating skills from lessons.
- **Relationships:** `memory-ledger.md` is its evidence ledger, with `MD` ids.

## 5. memory-ledger.md
- **Date/status:** Live scenarios run 2026-10-23. Group: Long-term memory.
- **What it records:** Decisions MD0–MD43 (at least), phase rows, a rename inventory, live scenarios M1–M18, a re-run after the base merge, and final qualification on the merged code.
- **Final state:** Every decision and scenario I saw is `passed`. M1–M18 pass, covering indexer search, the snapshot, concurrent updates (409 `memory_conflict`), restart resume, and the memory page at both viewport sizes.
- **Decisions seen:**
  - MD1: the indexer is bound through `CLIO_CTE_POOL`.

  - MD15: the marketplace `memory` plugin was deleted.
  - MD17: draft PRs are clio-agent#1835, gact-tui#674 and marketplace#110.
  - MD23: the opt-in explicit memory search injection was removed.
- **Builds on:** `long-term-memory-plan.md`.
- **Left open:**
  - M8 had no `explore` agent installed, so the check used a general subagent instead.
  - Platform rows are present, and there is a "Found outside this change" section. I did not read either.
- **Relationships:** The plan governs. This ledger overrides it where a decision row says the plan was wrong, per the plan's own rule.

## 6. science-ledger.md
- **Date/status:** Phase 0 exports from the `.cloud-run/phase0/` runs. Several rows still show `pending`. Group: Delegation, fork and science log.
- **What it records:** Decisions FD1–FD34, a subagent verdict table (FD13), a Phase 0 export baseline, and scenarios F1 onward. Prompts are labelled as mechanism (tool-directed) or plain request.
- **Final state, as far as I read:**
  - Passed: FD1, FD2, FD4, FD10–FD19, FD21–FD24 and FD29–FD34, and mechanism scenarios F1–F5.
  - Pending: FD3 (reframe approval), FD5–FD9, and FD20 (branch/PR setup).

- **Known limits stated:**

- **Builds on:** the plan, Addendum A, and the export design.
- **Left open:** F-scenario rows beyond F5 were not read.
- **Relationships:** It is the evidence ledger for the plan and the addendum.

weight.description: Relative flex weight of this component inside a Row or Column. Only meaningful as a direct child of one.

DataQuery.description: A server-side table query applied to dataUri: the table-query request body (POST /v1/artifacts/{id}/table-query) without format. The server runs filter, then aggregate, then downsample, then sort, then offset/limit. Omit columns to request every column of dataUri — except alongside aggregate, where columns is required, since aggregate's output columns (e.g. price_mean) don't exist in the source and so cannot be inferred. limit bounds the rows in ONE response (a transfer size), not the underlying data; offset pages through a larger result across several requests. When a chart or map query would otherwise exceed limit without an explicit downsample, the server instead samples evenly across the full range and reports that it did, rather than silently truncating to the first rows. limit's own maximum here is a generous safety ceiling, not the deployment's real per-response cap, which is server-configured. A viewer (e.g. an interactive data-table) may layer its own user-driven paging/filtering/sorting on top of this dataQuery without replacing it — the agent's own filter/aggregate/downsample intent still applies underneath. Shared verbatim by clio.chart.v1, clio.map.v1, and clio.data-table.v1.

GeoJsonGeometry.description: A GeoJSON Geometry object (RFC 7946 §3.1), strictly shaped: Point/MultiPoint/LineString/MultiLineString/Polygon/MultiPolygon carry coordinates; GeometryCollection carries geometries. Never a Feature/FeatureCollection, never a bare coordinate array.

quantity.description: Amount for baseAmount servings.

detail.description: Instruction that stays true at any scale. State fixed per-unit amounts here when needed; do not repeat the starting total or count.

quantity.description: Amount for the guide's baseAmount; the viewer rescales it with the control.

quantityUnit.description: Unit beside the scaled amount at quantity 1; use a singular countable label.

quantityUnitPlural.description: Optional label at other quantities, such as eggs or tubes; omit for invariant units.

category.description: Nominal group, such as station type. Use value for measured numbers.

value.description: Optional measured magnitude for a continuous colour scale and legend.

QueryAggregate.description: Group rows by groupBy (empty or omitted: one global group) and reduce; each metric becomes a result column named {column}_{fn}, which must not repeat a groupBy column.

QueryDownsample.description: How the server thins rows before limit applies. none keeps every row; stride keeps evenly spaced rows (per entityColumn up to maxPerEntity when set, else overall up to limit); per_entity_lttb runs LTTB on (x, y) per entityColumn (the whole table is one series without it) and needs x and y.

QueryFilter.description: One predicate; all filter entries are AND-ed. eq: value is a non-null scalar. in: value is a non-empty list of scalars. range: value is [min, max], inclusive, either side may be null. isnull: value omitted or true matches nulls, false matches non-nulls. contains: value is a non-empty string, matched as a case-insensitive substring of a string column (a per-column text filter).

QuerySort.description: One dataQuery.sort key; earlier entries in the list sort first.

SelectionState.description: The value at a bound selection path (/selection/<key>): the selected values of one data field. source is the id of the component that made the selection.

SpecDataNamedSource.description: Every `data` key anywhere in a Vega-Lite spec is absent or exactly {"name": "source"} — rows come from the component's data/dataUri, never the spec.

SpecNoBindElement.description: No `element` key inside any `bind` object (params[].bind.element) anywhere in a Vega-Lite spec, at any depth — it is a CSS selector that could mount a Vega input widget into any element on the host page, not just this chart.

SpecNoForbiddenKeys.description: No `url` or `usermeta` key anywhere in a Vega-Lite spec, at any depth.

time.description: ISO 8601 local date-time with an explicit UTC offset or Z.

data.description: Inline rows (at most 10000) — this array rides the surface's own wire message, so it is capped for transfer size; for a larger or growing dataset use dataUri instead, unbounded and paged/downsampled by the viewer. A cell is a scalar OR a strictly-shaped GeoJSON Geometry object ($defs/GeoJsonGeometry), so a geoshape mark can draw real shapes from inline rows.

spec.description: A Vega-Lite spec whose rows come from data/dataUri as the named dataset 'source' — the spec is chart configuration, never a data channel, and the dataset itself is unbounded via dataUri regardless of this cap. This schema already enforces the top-level key allowlist, no url/usermeta key at any depth, no bind.element at any depth (a CSS selector that could mount an input widget anywhere on the host page), and data only as {name: source} at any depth; the renderer additionally enforces the config-size (65536 bytes) and view-count (8) caps that keep the spec itself bounded and abuse-resistant, which JSON Schema cannot express. See a2ui/chart/guard_rules.json.

clio.mermaid.v1.description: Mermaid diagrams: workflows, protocols, ER/class models, states, git histories, grammars, trees and 33 supported families. Load this component for syntax and examples.

families.example:
flowchart LR
  raw[Raw input] --> check{Valid?}
  check -->|Yes| save[Save]
  check -->|No| repair[Repair]
  repair --> check
families.syntax: LR/RL/TB/BT set direction. id[Label], id{Decision}, --> edges, -->|condition| labelled edges; subgraph id[Label] ... end groups nodes. Stable IDs differ from display labels. classDef/class can mark semantic categories.

families.example:
sequenceDiagram
  actor Reader
  participant API
  Reader->>API: Request
  alt Allowed
    API-->>Reader: Record
  else Denied
    API-->>Reader: Error
  end
families.syntax: actor/participant name lifelines; ->> sends and -->> replies. alt condition / else condition / end is exclusive; opt, loop, par and critical blocks also end with end. activate/deactivate and Note over are available. A request and reply are separate messages.

families.example:
classDiagram
  class Sensor {
    +string id
    +read()
  }
  class Recorder
  Recorder "1" o-- "1..*" Sensor : reads
families.syntax: class Name { type field; method() } uses one member per line. <|-- inheritance, *-- composition, o-- aggregation, --> association; quoted multiplicities precede relation ends. + public, - private.

families.example:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Idle
  Idle --> Running : start
  Running --> Failed : error
  Failed --> Running : retry
  Running --> Complete : success
  Complete --> [*]
families.syntax: [*] is entry/exit; A --> B : trigger. state Label as ID gives aliases. Composite state ID { ... } nests transitions; <<choice>>, <<fork>>, <<join>> express branching. Do not confuse states with actions.

Entity { type name PK/FK } lists attributes. || exactly one, o| zero or one, }o/o{ zero or many, }|/|{ one or many. -- identifying, .. non-identifying; read the marker at each entity end independently. If an attribute type is not supplied, use an unspecified placeholder and explain it. Do not infer primary/foreign keys from names or add attributes to make an entity box look complete. Retain unknowns as unknowns.

families.example:
gantt
  dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
  section Trial
  Collect :a, 2026-10-01, 2d
  Analyse :b, after a, 3d
families.syntax: dateFormat controls input dates; section groups rows. Task :id,start,duration; after id starts after a dependency. done, active, crit and milestone are task tags. Use real dates/durations or label them illustrative.

families.example:
gitGraph
  commit id: "A"
  branch trial
  commit id: "B"
  checkout main
  commit id: "C"
  merge trial id: "M"
families.syntax: commit id: "label" creates a commit on the active branch. branch name creates/switches a branch; checkout name switches; merge name merges it into the active branch. cherry-pick id: copies a commit; tag/type are commit options. Preserve branching points, not just labels.
families.use: Commit ancestry, branch histories and merges.

families.example:
mindmap
  root((Study))
    Inputs
      Samples
      Metadata
    Outputs
      Report
families.syntax: Indentation determines parent/child structure. root((Label)) is a root shape; children may use [rectangle], (rounded), {{hexagon}}. Equal indentation means siblings; do not use it for message order.

families.example:
timeline
  title Trial history
  2025 : Pilot
  2026 : Replication : Review
families.syntax: title names the view; section groups periods. Period : event : another event associates events with a period. A following : event extends it.

families.example:
journey
  title Review experience
  section Evidence
    Find source: 3: Analyst
    Inspect result: 5: Analyst, Reviewer
families.syntax: section groups stages. Task: score: Actor, OtherActor gives a 1–5 experience score and responsible actors. Scores are not measured timings.

families.example:
pie title Synthetic allocation
  "Analysis" : 60
  "Review" : 40
families.syntax: pie title ... followed by "Category" : numericValue; showData shows values. Keep original units and denominators clear; use charts for linked data.

families.example:
quadrantChart
  x-axis Low effort --> High effort
  y-axis Low value --> High value
  quadrant-1 Plan
  quadrant-2 Prioritise
  quadrant-3 Defer
  quadrant-4 Reconsider
  Trial: [0.3, 0.8]
families.syntax: x-axis Low --> High and y-axis Low --> High label axes; quadrant-1..4 label regions. Item: [x,y] places a point with coordinates in [0,1].
families.use: Items positioned on two qualitative axes.

families.example:
xychart-beta
  x-axis [A, B, C]
  y-axis "Count" 0 --> 10
  bar [3, 7, 5]
families.syntax: x-axis [categories] or a numeric range; y-axis title min --> max; bar [values] and line [values]. Array positions must match x values.

requirement ID { id: ...; text: ...; risk: low/medium/high; verifymethod: test/analysis/inspection/demonstration } uses separate lines. element ID { type: ... } names evidence/system elements. A - satisfies -> B (also verifies, traces, refines, contains, copies, derives).

families.example:
sankey-beta
Input,Accepted,8
Input,Rejected,2
Accepted,Report,8
families.syntax: After the declaration, CSV rows are source,target,value. Quote names containing commas. Edge width represents the numeric value; use consistent units.

families.example:
architecture-beta
  group lab(cloud)[Lab]
  service api(server)[API] in lab
  service db(database)[Store] in lab
  api:R -- L:db
families.syntax: group id(icon)[Label]; service id(icon)[Label] in groupId. Built-in icons include cloud, database, disk, server, internet. a:R -- L:b connects right/left ports; :T/:B top/bottom; arrows add direction. These symbols are not connections to real services.

families.example:
C4Context
  Person(reader, "Reader")
  System(catalog, "Catalog")
  Rel(reader, catalog, "Finds evidence")
families.syntax: Person(id,"Label"), System(id,"Label"), Container(id,"Label","Tech"), Component(id,"Label","Tech"), Rel(a,b,"Purpose"). Boundaries use braces. C4Dynamic uses ordered Rel calls; Deployment_Node contains Container instances. Do not mix context systems with deployment nodes without explaining the level.
families.use: Architecture at a declared level of abstraction.

families.example:
block-beta
  columns 2
  a["Acquire"] b["Analyse"]
  c["Review"]:2
  a --> c
  b --> c
families.syntax: columns N sets columns; id[Label]:span spans columns; space reserves a cell. block:group ... end nests blocks; A --> B adds relationships. Use this when explicit grouping matters more than automatic graph layout.

families.example:
packet-beta
  0-3: "Version"
  4-7: "Flags"
  8-15: "Length"
families.syntax: start-end: "Field" assigns an inclusive bit range; +N: "Field" appends N bits. Preserve field widths and ordering. It does not model message exchanges.

families.example:
kanban
  todo[To do]
    clean[Clean samples]
  done[Done]
    collect[Collect samples]
families.syntax: ColumnID[Column label] at one indent, cardID[Card label] beneath it. Card metadata can set assigned, ticket and priority. It illustrates state; it does not create CLIO tasks or make cards a live task board.

families.example:
radar-beta
  axis q["Quality"], s["Speed"], c["Coverage"]
  curve a["Trial A"]{8, 4, 6}
  max 10
families.syntax: axis id1["Label"], id2["Label"]; curve series["Label"]{values}; max N sets the scale. Values follow axis order. Do not invent normalized scores.

families.example:
treemap-beta
  "Work"
    "Analysis": 6
    "Review": 4
families.syntax: Indent "Group" headings and "Leaf": value children. Area represents the numeric weight, not temporal order; preserve the hierarchy and units.

Choose one notation. EBNF: name = expression ;, quoted terminals, bare rule references, adjacency sequence, | choice, [x] optional, (x) grouping, x* zero-or-more, x+ one-or-more. ABNF: name = expression, / choice, [x] optional, *x zero-or-more, 1*x one-or-more, %x41 hex terminal. ABNF quoted literals are case-insensitive; for exact ASCII case use %x byte sequences, e.g. %x4F.50.45.4E for OPEN. This pinned renderer does not accept RFC 7405 %s/%i prefixes. EBNF/PEG quoted literals are case-sensitive; identical displayed labels do not prove language equivalence. PEG: name <- expression ;, / ordered choice, x? optional, x* and x+ repetition, &x/!x lookahead; quote terminals. End productions with ; in each notation in this renderer. The railroad DSL uses name = terminal("word") ; with nonterminal("rule"), sequence(...), choice(...), optional(...), zeroOrMore(...) and oneOrMore(...). Do not mix operators; define referenced rules and preserve optionality.
families.use: Accepted token sequences in a grammar.

families.syntax: Flowchart-like direction, nodes and edges, with semantic shapes @{ type: input/tool/action/refdoc/decision/task }. --> is sequence; reference/failure links have different meaning. This is a diagram, not an agent execution or task submission mechanism.
families.use: Agent actions, tools, inputs and reference documents.

families.example:
treeView-beta
  study/
    data/
      readings.csv
    report.md
families.syntax: Indent children beneath parents; a trailing / denotes a directory. A file has no trailing /. ## description annotates an entry. Preserve names/extensions; displaying a file does not grant/open it.

families.example:
cynefin-beta
  complex
    "Explore hypothesis"
  clear
    "Apply checklist"
families.syntax: complex/complicated/clear/chaotic/confusion headings with indented "Item" labels. domain --> domain : label marks a transition. Domains express the decision context, not measured risk scores.
families.use: Classify decisions by the Cynefin domains.

families.example:
wardley-beta
  anchor Reader [0.95, 0.5]
  component Report [0.8, 0.6]
  component Storage [0.2, 0.85]
  Reader -> Report
  Report -> Storage
families.syntax: anchor Name [visibility,evolution]; component Name [visibility,evolution]; A -> B is a dependency; evolve Name target proposes evolution. Coordinates are in [0,1]; label hypothetical positions as estimates.

families.example:
eventmodeling
  tf 01 ui ReviewUI
  tf 02 cmd SubmitReview
  tf 03 evt ReviewSubmitted
  tf 04 rmo ReviewList
families.syntax: tf frame kind Name defines a frame; kinds ui, cmd, evt, rmo, pcr identify user interface, command, event, read model, processor. [[dataName]] references a data block. Frame order is chronology, not a generic causal arrow between arbitrary nodes.
families.use: Commands, events and read models over chronological frames.

families.example:
usecase-beta
  actor reader("Reader")
  inspect("Inspect evidence")
  reader --> inspect
families.syntax: actor id("Label"), goal("Label"); systemBoundary id[Label] ... end groups goals. actor --> goal associates them. include/extend relate use cases; inheritance is different from a sequential workflow.
families.use: Actors and goals within a system boundary.

families.example:
venn-beta
  set A[Reviewed]:8
  set B[Published]:6

families.syntax: The declaration alone renders version/diagnostic information. Use only when diagnosing the viewer, not as a diagram of user data.

host: Use source OR dataUri, never both. dataUri uses the actual returned artifact URI of a registered UTF-8 source file. Where the producer accepts a workspace file path, it registers that file before validation; reuse its returned URI. Do not guess artifact IDs or use HTTP URLs. source can be a dynamic string binding; the bound value is diagram text.

Render requested diagrams with the declared A2UI surface tools, including inline chat explanations. A mermaid fenced block displays source code, not a rendered visual; use it when the user asks for source or Markdown export. If rendering is unavailable, report the limitation. Use the declared dashboard tools for a saved composed report. Do not install Pele, import JavaScript, or invent clio.pele.v1.

CLIO supplies theme colours and adaptive container width. Renderer options maxWidth, responsive, config, themeVariables and custom CSS are not component properties. Mermaid init directives, HTML labels, arbitrary callbacks and external images/links are rejected. Text line breaks use literal backslash-n inside labels (encoded as \\n in JSON); source statements use JSON \n.

Navigation: add a standalone flowchart line: click data "workspace-folder:data/inputs" "Open inputs". data must be an existing node; the relative directory must exist in the current workspace. Encode reserved path characters. The host opens Files using existing access. This does not run code, create a folder, or grant permissions. Plain exports do not provide workspace navigation.

The component has source view, zoom, pan, expand, copy, SVG/PNG/source export and selection/reference controls supplied by the viewer. Do not add fake toolbar properties. Tree filenames, architecture services and git commits are diagram text; they do not automatically become file navigation.

Preserve semantics before styling: branch conditions, message order, entity cardinality, grammar repetition and hierarchy are different relationships. Use clio.chart.v1 for data-backed quantitative views needing units, filters or shared selection; Mermaid chart families remain available for small self-contained illustrations. Use graph views for exploratory node networks.

Review the actual published artifact: inspect its captured image at the docked width and expanded when useful, including titles, text, arrows and legends. Fix clipping, tiny text, lost edges or misleading relationships and capture again. A valid schema, accepted source or SVG is not a visual pass. If capture is unavailable, report that specific gap. The shared review-visual-presentation skill supplies the capture workflow.

On an error, repair the actual declaration, quoting, indentation, block endings or operators; preserve difficult relationships. CLIO can fall back to Mermaid for legacy syntax, but Pele-only declarations need Pele. Do not silently replace the diagram with an unrelated gallery. External Mermaid plugins such as ZenUML and custom icon resolvers are not exposed.

source_encoding.rule: The source value contains actual line breaks between statements. JSON encodes each newline once as \n. Do not double-escape them as \\n, which leaves backslash and n characters in the source. When writing JSON from Python/JavaScript, construct a multiline source string and serialize the document once. Label-internal backslash-n is a different syntax.

clio.mesh-viewport.v1.description: An orbitable 3D view of a registered standard mesh or a CLIO FEA mesh with optional result fields.

clio.message-draft.v1.description: Editable alternatives for an email, chat message, or text, with copy and open actions.

clio.metric.v1.description: One labeled number, optionally with a unit and trend.

clio.progress.v1.description: A bounded or indeterminate operation's progress.

clio.raster-viewport.v1.description: An interactive viewport for a registered two-dimensional grid, with sampled values, colour scale, and region reference.

clio.slider.v1.description: A fractional-step numeric control, or a two-value range, with typed value boxes.

clio.status.v1.description: A single labeled state, e.g. a running step.

clio.steps.v1.description: An interactive protocol or recipe with checkable actions, timers, and separately scaled ingredients.

observedAt.description: ISO 8601 local date-time with an explicit UTC offset or Z.

clio.weather.v1.description: Current weather and hourly or daily forecasts for a field site or location.

dataUri.description: A workspace file path or artifact:// reference; CLIO registers a path as an artifact before validation. A JSON file shaped {"nodes": [...], "edges": [...]}.

nodes.description: Inline nodes (at most 128) — rides the surface's own wire message; give edges too, or use dataUri instead of both for a larger graph, unbounded.

allOf.description: Exactly one of nodes+edges or dataUri is required.

clio.workflow.v1.description: A step/edge graph showing a multi-step plan's progress.

file.description: CLIO scientific-agent A2UI components, including interactive data views and widgets.

and.description: Performs a logical AND operation on a list of boolean values.

values.description: The list of boolean values to evaluate.

email.description: Checks that the value is a valid email address.

focusWorkflow.description: Focuses one node of a clio.workflow.v1 component.

stepId.description: The workflow node id to focus.

formatCurrency.description: Formats a number as a currency string.

decimals.description: Optional. The number of decimal places to show. Defaults to 0 or 2 depending on locale.

grouping.description: Optional. If true, uses locale-specific grouping separators (e.g. '1,000'). If false, returns raw digits (e.g. '1000'). Defaults to true.

formatDate.description: Formats a timestamp into a string using a pattern.

format.description:
A Unicode TR35 date pattern string.

Token Reference:
- Year: 'yy' (26), 'yyyy' (2026)
- Month: 'M' (1), 'MM' (01), 'MMM' (Jan), 'MMMM' (January)
- Day: 'd' (1), 'dd' (01), 'E' (Tue), 'EEEE' (Tuesday)
- Hour (12h): 'h' (1-12), 'hh' (01-12) - requires 'a' for AM/PM
- Hour (24h): 'H' (0-23), 'HH' (00-23) - Military Time
- Minute: 'mm' (00-59)
- Second: 'ss' (00-59)
- Period: 'a' (AM/PM)

Examples:
- 'MMM dd, yyyy' -> 'Jan 16, 2026'
- 'HH:mm' -> '14:30' (Military)
- 'h:mm a' -> '2:30 PM'
- 'EEEE, d MMMM' -> 'Friday, 16 January'

formatNumber.description: Formats a number with the specified grouping and decimal precision.

decimals.description: Optional. The number of decimal places to show. Defaults to 0 or 2 depending on locale.

grouping.description: Optional. If true, uses locale-specific grouping separators (e.g. '1,000'). If false, returns raw digits (e.g. '1000'). Defaults to true.

formatString.description: Performs string interpolation of data model values and other functions in the catalog functions list and returns the resulting string. The value string can contain interpolated expressions in the `${expression}` format. Supported expression types include: JSON Pointer paths to the data model (e.g., `${/absolute/path}` or `${relative/path}`), and client-side function calls (e.g., `${now()}`). Function arguments must be named (e.g., `${formatDate(value:${/currentDate}, format:'MM-dd')}`). To include a literal `${` sequence, escape it as `\${`.

not.description: Performs a logical NOT operation on a boolean value.

openArtifact.description: Opens a registered artifact in the workspace artifact viewer.

uri.description: The artifact:// or resource:// URI to open.

openUrl.description: Opens the specified URL in a browser or handler. This function has no return value.

or.description: Performs a logical OR operation on a list of boolean values.

values.description: The list of boolean values to evaluate.

pluralize.description: Returns a localized string based on the Common Locale Data Repository (CLDR) plural category of the count (zero, one, two, few, many, other). Requires an 'other' fallback. For English, just use 'one' and 'other'.

few.description: String for the 'few' category (e.g., small groups in Slavic languages).

many.description: String for the 'many' category (e.g., large groups in various languages).

other.description: The default/fallback string (used for general plural cases).

two.description: String for the 'two' category (used in Arabic, Welsh, etc.).

value.description: The numeric value used to determine the plural category.

regex.description: Checks that the value matches a regular expression string.

pattern.description: The regex pattern to match against.

required.description: Checks that the value is not null, undefined, or empty.

selectData.description: Writes a selection to the data model: a SelectionState {field, values: rowIds, source: 'selectData'} at path. Every component whose selection is bound to that path follows it.

field.description: The data field the row identifiers are values of.

path.description: The data-model path the selection is written to, /selection/<key>: the same path the linked components bind their selection to.

rowIds.description: The selected row identifiers; written as the values.

surfaceId.description: The surface the selection applies to; defaults to the current surface.
