## Context

The v0.10 program (docs/design/v010-program-2026-08.md on develop, `1c8e39fd`) integrates
four streams into one coherent system: MCP 2026-07-28 compliance, clio-relay federation
(agents AND scientific applications), the mcp_ui_sciences interaction semantics, and the
Session v3 UI prototype — across iowarp/clio-agent and iowarp/gact-tui. All owner decisions
are closed (D1 multi-connection client/no hub; D2 shared schema package with generated TS
types; D3 Codex workhorse via codex-plugin-cc, verified live). This planning pass produces
the COMPLETE slice tree so that plan approval = mint every issue (umbrella + 5 phase parents
+ slices, cross-repo) and start P0 immediately.

**Goal state after approval:** issue tree live in both repos (+ relay-side asks), each slice
issue carrying: scope, acceptance (verifiable), failing-first test intent, deletions,
dependencies, size (S/M/L), lane (codex/claude/either). Execution starts with P0.

## Execution model (locked, applies to every slice)

- One slice = one issue = one branch = one PR; failing-first regression tests; no silent
  fallbacks (typed reasons); deletions land with replacements.
- **Fable (me): orchestration, all merges, final review of every diff, gate verdicts.**
  Claude tokens are preserved for this — implementation is delegated wherever possible.
- **Codex (gpt-5.6-sol default, via the verified codex-plugin-cc runtime): default
  implementer** for well-specified slices — `task --write` per slice in its own worktree,
  `--background` for parallel lanes (≤2-3 concurrent; one shared subscription meter).
- **Claude workflows (opus/sonnet/haiku by difficulty)**: design-heavy slices, wide
  mechanical fan-outs (sonnet/haiku), and all adversarial reviews of Codex diffs.
- **Cross-vendor review both directions**: Codex diffs → Claude adversarial review;
  Claude diffs → `/codex:adversarial-review`. Review-gate stays manual (explicit calls).
- Phase boundaries are hard gates (unit/CI + the phase's live gate) before the next phase's
  slices open. Visual harness gates P4 surfaces incrementally once it exists.

## Phase structure (from the program doc — slice trees below filled by this pass)

- P0 Foundations — decomposition re-land, MCP client factory, fastmcp4 spike, bearer
  scheme, clio-schemas bootstrap, (already landed: #1031 harness).
- P1 MCP v2 compliance — per-request caps, server/discover, MRTR, elicitation→HITL,
  SEP-2663 tasks client, wire cancel, prompts/get, MCP auth, legacy matrix, typed degrades.
- P2 Unified invoker + federation — shared schemas, ExpertInvoker (#671), relay transport,
  one spawn surface, runs registry, message-an-agent, remote applications (remote MCP
  federation, JARVIS/Spack, exit injections, execution views), relay-side asks.
- P3 Interaction + artifact surfaces — P3.0 contract adoption (mcp_ui_sciences upstream
  spec), MCP Apps renderer, A2UI catalogs ported, Live Web artifacts, documents floor,
  THE annotation primitive, interaction cards v2, private-data slots, teardown.
- P4 Session v3 UI — component kit + conformance guard first, then shell/transcript/
  composer+trays/detail-slot/observability/settings+registries; multi-connection client;
  per-slice deletion of old surfaces; GACT v0.3 SPEC.
- P5 Acceptance + release — visual harness (web + desktop lanes, prototype = render spec),
  through-the-UI semantics verification, composed live gates (EarthScope + federation +
  mcp_ui_sciences scenarios + 1031 verdict), deletion audit, release v0.10.0.

## 0. The one-sentence thesis

One spawn primitive, one task record, one artifact record, two transports (local, relay),
one part grammar on the wire, one component kit in the client — MCP v2 semantics end to end,
rendered by the Session v3 UI.

## 1. Program structure decision

**ONE program umbrella, five phase subtrees, strictly gated phase boundaries.**

- One parent issue in clio-agent (`v0.10 program`) whose children are five phase parents;
  each phase parent owns an ordered slice tree. gact-tui gets one mirrored umbrella whose
  children are the client slices of P3/P4/P5 (same numbering, cross-linked).
- Rationale: the pillars share three schema decisions (task record, artifact record, part
  grammar) — separate campaigns would re-litigate them (the unified-design rule). But phases
  are real sequencing boundaries with their own gates, so the tree gives per-phase workflows
  without splitting design authority.
- Version semantics: P0–P2 ship as 0.10.0-alpha tags off develop as they gate; v0.10.0 cuts
  after P5. Nothing merges to main until the program's composed gate is green.

## 2. Owner decisions baked in (from 2026-07-29 review)

1. Documents and Live Web are IN scope (Monday meeting feature ask; "full web semantic" for
   sharable interactive reports). Office rendering = model-rendered floor; builder/LibreOffice
   is a designed-for extension, not built now. Email integration = future pillar, seams only.
2. Sampling pillar dead (deprecated in MCP v2); its use case (visual elements requesting model
   output) rides the MCP Apps bridge + MRTR/task input rounds.
3. No hardcoding prototype semantics one-by-one; general capabilities instead
   (message-an-agent covers steer/queue/wake; placement covers local/remote spawn).
4. UI is a unification point: component kit first, every surface is composition; a
   kit-conformance check guards it.
5. One spawn primitive — `relay_submit_agent`-style split tools are deletion targets.
6. MCP v2 compliance is a program goal in itself (research directions ride the task system).

**Open owner decisions this doc forces (full context so they are decidable):**

- **D1 — multi-backend topology (DECIDED 2026-07-30, owner correction).** Primary agents
  and subagents are DIFFERENT things and use different transports:
  - **Primary agents** = full gact backends on reachable endpoints. gact-tui becomes a
    MULTI-CONNECTION client: today's single connection (base URL + SSE + cursor state)
    becomes a first-class connection object and the UI holds several. Tunnels are
    USER-PROVIDED (ssh -L port-forward, LAN, VPN) — the app never proxies or federates
    gact-to-gact; there is NO hub module. Every session is homed on exactly one backend;
    rail/runs/search views are client-side unions. The prototype's "agents" registry is
    this connection list; its Backends page ("ssh tunnel · contract v0.2") is its status.
  - **Remote subagents/applications** = children a session's OWN BACKEND runs through
    clio-relay semantics (P2). The browser never speaks to a relay.
  Verified server support (audit 2026-07-30): contract handshake EXISTS
  (`GET /v1/capabilities` → contract_version + AuthInfo, routes/system.py:435); CORS
  opt-in EXISTS (`gact.cors.origins`, app.py:1219-1233, deny-by-default); auth is the one
  gap — AuthInfo advertises a `schemes` LIST (types.py:149) but only `trust_socket` is
  implemented. Slices: (a) server `bearer` scheme behind the existing advertisement
  (config token, constant-time compare) for non-loopback backends — SSH-forwarded/local
  stay trust_socket; (b) client connection objects + per-connection capabilities check
  with loud refusal on contract mismatch; (c) docs for the CORS knob (web build only).

- **D2 — shared schema home.** TaskRecord/ArtifactRef/ArtifactUse/part shapes must be
  byte-compatible across THREE consumers: clio-agent (python), clio-relay (python,
  `extra="forbid"` strict), gact-tui (TypeScript render types). Two ways:
  - **Option A — shared schema package (RECOMMENDED).** A tiny `clio-schemas` (name TBD)
    package: pydantic models + exported JSON Schema; clio-agent and clio-relay depend on it;
    gact-tui GENERATES its TS types from the exported JSON Schema in CI. Pros: one source of
    truth; the TS-generation kills an entire class of wire drift; growth-friendly (parts,
    provenance, runs will join). Cons: a third release artifact to version; relay pins can
    lag a rev; cross-repo version-bump choreography.
  - **Option B — duplicated models + CI equality tests.** Each repo keeps its own models and
    commits an exported JSON Schema snapshot; each CI diff-tests its snapshot against the
    other repo's committed snapshot; drift = red build. Pros: no new package; relay stays
    fully self-contained (its stated client-agnostic stance). Cons: every schema change is a
    two-repo lockstep dance; gact-tui types still need a generation source; equality tests
    rot if the snapshot-refresh flow is manual.
  **DECIDED 2026-07-30 (owner: "whatever is more correct, regardless of work"): Option A.**
  One canonical schema package; pydantic models + exported JSON Schema; clio-agent and
  clio-relay depend on it; gact-tui generates TS types from the JSON Schema in CI.
- **D3 — Codex as the implementation workhorse** (RESOLVED 2026-07-30; owner motivation is
  TOKEN ECONOMY — far larger Codex allowance with full refreshes — not capability). Primary
  mechanism: the OFFICIAL OpenAI Claude Code plugin **`openai/codex-plugin-cc`** (released
  2026-03-30; owner installed 2026-07-30, active after session restart). It registers
  `/codex:rescue` (delegate a task; `--background/--wait/--resume/--model/--effort`),
  `/codex:review` + `/codex:adversarial-review` (read-only, `--base <ref>`), `/codex:transfer`
  (hand a whole session to a persistent Codex thread), `/codex:status|result|cancel`, and a
  `codex-rescue` subagent; under the hood it brokers a persistent Codex app-server session
  and inherits `codex login` subscription auth.
  Division of labor: **Codex (gpt-5.6 tiers via --model; verify exposed IDs post-install) is
  the DEFAULT implementer** for well-specified slices — dispatched per-slice in git worktrees
  via `/codex:rescue --background`; **Claude/Fable owns orchestration, all merges, the
  hard-taste slices, and review**. ALL reviews are cross-vendor: Codex-authored diffs get
  Claude adversarial review; Claude-authored diffs get `/codex:adversarial-review`.
  Token-economy reality check: every Codex mode (plugin/CLI/exec/SDK) draws ONE shared plan
  meter (rolling ~5h window + weekly cap; parallel workers burn it faster, they don't
  multiply capacity) — so fan-out stays moderate (2-3 background rescues), and the win is
  SHIFTING implementation tokens to the Codex meter, not parallel scale. Budget context at
  Codex's real ~272K cap. Fallbacks if the plugin misbehaves: official Codex SDK
  (@openai/codex-sdk / openai-codex python) or `codex exec --json --output-schema`; NEVER
  Codex native subagents for Sol/Terra (encrypted parent→subagent delegation kills the audit
  trail). Codex-as-MCP-tasks-client remains unconfirmed — nothing depends on it.

- P0.3 fastmcp 4.x migration spike: our servers (fs/shell/gateway) + client on the 4.0 line;

- P0.4 Land the rescued #1031 gate harness (PR #1095) + fold its synthetic blueprints into

### P1 — MCP v2 compliance (the protocol floor)
Client: per-request `_meta` capabilities + `server/discover`; MRTR handling (InputRequired →
retry-with-inputResponses); elicitation handler bridged into the EXISTING gact HITL/questions
pipeline (one surface, form + url modes); tasks extension client (CreateTaskResult on any
augmentable call, tasks/get poll with pollIntervalMs, input_required rounds via tasks/update,
durable task-id persistence for crash recovery, Mcp-Name routing header, cooperative cancel);
wire cancellation for foreground calls; prompts/get; MCP auth for remote servers (headers on
runtime-dict specs + OAuth); `-32021/-32022` error handling; resultType tolerance for legacy
servers. Server: our FastMCP servers speak 2026-07-28 through fastmcp 4; tasks NOT enabled on
our servers yet (no use case; relay owns durable tasks).
- Every degrade typed (stream_fallback catalog extension for MCP-path downgrades).
- Gate: conformance suite vs a fastmcp 4 reference server + clio-relay v1.5.9 (tasks
  round-trip incl. input_required + reconnect-by-task-id); legacy matrix green.

### P2 — Unified invoker + federation (the spine; absorbs #948 remnants + #671)
- P2.1 Shared schemas (D2): TaskRecord aligned to relay's job/task projection semantics
  (taskId=jobId, working/input_required/completed/failed/cancelled, terminal⇔state,
  isError-in-completed); ArtifactRef/ArtifactUse strict-match tests against relay models
  (64-hex sha256, closed evidence enum, extra=forbid). Cross-repo schema-equality tests in
  both CIs; drift = red build.
- P2.2 ExpertInvoker boundary (#671): `invoke(expert_ref, request) → result/stream`,
  serializable records, local transport = today's in-process path re-expressed.
- P2.3 Relay transport: submit as relay job (MCP tasks client from P1), stream/poll handles,
  reconstruct after detach; two auth doors hidden behind one client module.
- P2.4 ONE spawn surface: placement as parameter/policy; delete split tools; runs registry +
  API (async/detached/parallel runs; local and remote uniform); run-handle parts on the wire.
- P2.5 Message-an-agent primitive: queue/steer/wake unified (local = queue injection at step
  boundary; remote = tasks/update input round); parent supersede notification as event.
- P2.6 Relay-side asks (filed on iowarp/clio-relay, not blocking): per-user identity story,
  post-admission elicitation producer, remote_agent JARVIS package, schema adoption rev.
- P2.7 Remote APPLICATION semantics (co-equal with remote agents — relay is a scientific-
  computing federation layer, not an agent-spawner): (a) remote MCP federation — allowlisted
  cluster-side MCP servers projected as local namespaced tools backed by durable `mcp_call`
  jobs (relay's remote-mcp-federation contract); (b) application deployment + execution —
  JARVIS/Spack pipelines as durable jobs (`jarvis` job kind): deploy, run, live progress
  events, scheduler identity (slurm native_id), log/artifact retrieval, detach-keeps-running;
  (c) background-exit injections — a remote application ending becomes a typed injected part
  in the owning turn; (d) live execution views fed by the task-timeline event stream.
- Gate (composed, stresses ALL of it — not just agent spawn): on a real cluster target via
  relay, one scenario runs (1) a local child and a relay child with identical part grammar,
  (2) a remote MCP tool call through the federation path, (3) a JARVIS application deployment
  (ParaView or LAMMPS — reuse the proven cc_dispatch/mcp_ui_sciences session recipes) with
  live progress, detach, reconnect-by-task-id, and background-exit injection, and (4) an
  artifact minted remotely carrying the converged ArtifactRef + full lineage. The
  mcp_ui_sciences evidence bundles (evidence/fastmcp-sep2663/, released against relay
  v1.5.9) are the reference transcripts for what "good" looks like.

- P3.1 MCP Apps renderer (gact-tui): sandbox-proxy + CSP builder pattern, AppBridge JSON-RPC,

- P3.3 Live Web artifacts: agent-authored HTML/React artifacts as first-class ui_payload

  network + user-granted exact origins (rides #974 egress), kill/disable. Design workspace
  (visual editor) explicitly deferred to post-0.10.
- P3.4 SUPPORTED artifacts — the MUST is UI-level artifact INTERACTION, not viewing
  (owner, 2026-07-30). "Supported" means: an agent-created artifact is viewable in the UI
  AND the user can act on its content — highlight a span, get a popup, type a comment, and
  the agent receives a message carrying the anchored context (artifact id + revision +
  quoted span/location + the user's text). Document rendering is the foundation because
  most artifacts are documents.
  - **The annotation primitive (one, shared across kinds):** anchored-context messages.
    Anchor types per kind — text span (markdown, code, logs, answer messages), PDF
    text-layer span, table cell/range (csv/profile views), element ref (html/live-web
    surfaces — the prototype's floating selected-element box is this same primitive),
    region (images/plots, later). Anchors bind artifact + revision + content hash so a
    comment can never silently point at drifted bytes; stale anchors are surfaced, not
    remapped silently. Selection alone stays local; only explicit submission creates the
    agent message (a typed part on the wire — goes in the GACT v0.3 SPEC). The agent's
    response typically lands as a new revision of the same artifact, closing the loop.
  - **Rendering floor (prerequisite):** markdown → trusted DOM; PDF → pinned self-hosted
    viewer with real text layer; sanitized static HTML/SVG (non-executing allowlist);
    office/opendocument (docx/xlsx/pptx/odt/ods/odp) rendered + downloadable as canonical
    bytes. Revisions + provenance identical to every other artifact kind.
  - **Deferred tier (standing open issue, designed-for now):** offline LibreOffice/Docker
    builder, WOPI/OnlyOffice live editing — the issue links the working
    cc_dispatch/mcp_ui_sciences reference code (host/src/host/document_runtime.py ~3000
    LOC, document-runtime/ Docker builder, WOPI plumbing app.py:1162-1477). The artifact
    record + renderer registry + anchor model must accept these without schema change.
  - Gate addition: the P3 scenario includes the full loop live — agent writes a markdown
    report artifact; user highlights a paragraph, comments; agent receives the anchored
    message and revises; the UI shows the new revision with the comment resolved against it.
- P3.5 Interaction cards v2: ask card (multi-select, per-option notes, custom scope, decline),
  permission card states, MCP elicitation rendered through the same cards.
- Gate: the cc_dispatch demo-session library is the scenario source — the repo has BUILT
  sessions demonstrating exactly these surfaces (ParaView mcp-app viewer, LAMMPS runs,
  Darshan mcpui widgets, live executions, A2UI scientific widgets, document artifacts).
  The P3 gate re-runs a curated set of those scenarios against the NEW stack: MCP App
  (ParaView), A2UI (Darshan/science widgets), Live Web report, and each document format,

## 3b. The gact-tui side is a CONTRACT change, not just new screens (GACT v0.3)

The program cuts a new wire-contract SPEC in gact-tui (the gact-tui#318 pattern: SPEC issue +
locked doc), version-bumped from the current contract. The UI work in P3/P4 consumes these
server-side semantic changes — enumerated here so the client scope is visible:

- **New/extended part kinds on the wire:** run-handle fields on task/tool parts (handle id,
  run label, live states, host); injection parts (background-exit + steering injections);
  a2ui/mcp-app parts (already partly present) with pin/scrub actions; ask parts with
  multi-select options, per-option notes, custom scope, decline; placement/host on task
  parts. All additive; each lands with schema in the SPEC + fixture parity tests.
- **New APIs the UI consumes:** runs registry (list/detach/dismiss, live tickers);
  agents/relays/backends registry CRUD + status (D1 hub); artifact detail payloads for the
  provenance/recreate tabs (lineage route, version record, transform record, reproduce
  bundle — projections of shipped #966 modules); observability projections (timeline/gantt
  rows, session-wide tool aggregation, per-turn artifact attribution, context/cost stats);
  steering/queue APIs (per-child queue CRUD, deliver-now, interrupt, wake); settings-backed
  routes for every settings page that ships visible (unbacked pages ship hidden).
- **Render-contract regeneration:** CANONICAL-CONVERSATION.md and the pre-#880 visual
  fixtures are superseded; P4 locks a CANONICAL-SESSION-V3 contract generated from live
  wire captures of the gate scenarios, and the P5.1 visual harness enforces it.
- **Client deletions:** the old surface set is enumerated and deleted per-slice as v3
  surfaces gate (no dual UI, no legacy render paths kept "just in case").

{"path": "/home/user/clio-agent/.cloud-run/f17/ws-f17-docs/design/governance-surfaces-2026-07.md", "size_bytes": 29199, "content": "# Governance surfaces on one engine: hooks + planning mode

> **STATUS: FINAL** (grounded + adversarially reviewed + owner decisions resolved). Baseline
> `develop @ be24b6ec` (v0.8.1, post-#1031). One combined campaign, four slice-groups
> (P0 engine → P1 planning → P2 hooks), sequenced so P1/P2 ride the P0 uplift. Deletion-first.
> Companion research: `docs/design/hooks-research-2026-07.md`,
> `docs/design/planning-mode-research-2026-07.md`.

## Context

Campaign items #3 (Hooks) and #4 (Planning mode) are **the same feature seen twice.** clio has
**three half-built governance surfaces** — the permission engine, plan mode, and hooks — and each
independently wants *declarative, priority-ordered, tighten-only, annotation-aware,
mode/event-scoped policy on one engine.* Today each expresses that as bespoke hardcoded Python or
dead scaffolding. Both research surveys independently concluded plan-mode ACL and hooks policy
should be **one engine with one priority model**, and that engine is the #1031 `grant_resolver`.

Grounded state (three probes, file:line-verified; confirmed by an adversarial review):
- **Engine** (`grant_resolver`): `resolve()` is **first-match over an unordered append list** — no
  priority bands; `mode` is a literal unused placeholder (`grant_resolver.py:194`); the plan lock
  beats policy only by code-order accident; the `fs_root` projection is **dead**
  (`resolve("fs_root",…)` = zero call sites); no annotation source-of-truth; `GrantRecord.kind` is
  trivially extensible.
- **Plan mode**: MODE is the **same read-only predicate copy-pasted into three modules**
  (`permission_gate.py:499`, `enrichment.py:300`, `proposal_effects.py:187`); no
  repo-tracked-mutation carve-out (can't even run `git status`); `chat` mode is a documented lie
  (no code checks it). PROMPT is **dead-wired** (`session.mode` plumbed to every `forward()` then
  `del`'d at `builders.py:275/1365/1792`; denial message generic). ARTIFACT/EXIT/TODO are zeros.
- **Hooks**: a **dead `/v1/hooks` CRUD stub** (right shape, zero execution) and a **live-but-partial
  in-process registry** (`runtime/hooks.py`: `post_tool`/`on_error` dead, `pre_message` transform
  fictional, **hook-failure reasons dropped** at `permission_gate.py:479-480` — violating "hook
  failure ≠ user rejection" in shipped code, and `pre_tool` fires *before* `is_read_only`, letting a
  hook gate a provably-read-only call). `ToolRuntimeHooks.tool_interceptor` (full synthesize/mutate)
  is fully wired through the dispatch boundary with **no producer**.

So: **build one governance engine and express plan mode and hooks as data on it, deleting the three
bespoke encodings and both old hook systems.** Deletion over forced reuse (owner).

---

## Pillar 0 — Engine uplift (the shared seam)

**Delete inventory.** `resolve()`'s first-match `return`-on-first-hit; the hardcoded 3× plan lock
(re-expressed as data in P1.1); any bash-safety heuristic residue (verify #1032 removed it — do
**not** reintroduce one).

**Design.**
- **P0.1 Priority bands + merge rule.** Add `priority: int` to the policy row and `GrantRecord`.
  `resolve()` evaluates *all* matching rows sorted by priority and applies **most-restrictive-wins**
  (`deny > defer > ask > modify > allow`); `additionalContext` from all matches concatenates; two
  `modify` matches is an **error**, not last-writer-wins. **Migration (the golden-test key):**
  existing rows get **unique descending priorities by insertion index** — a stable sort then
  reproduces today's first-match order exactly, so most-restrictive-merge only ever applies to *new*
  same-band rules and today's policies resolve **identically** (regression-pinned).
- **P0.2 Real `mode` + `event` axes + new kinds.** Thread `mode` through `_scope_matches` as a real
  dimension (rows carry `modes: list[str]`) and add an `event` axis (rows carry `on: list[str]`), so
  plan-mode rules (`modes=[plan]`) and hook rules (`on=[PreToolUse]`) are ordinary grant rows.
  `GrantRecord.kind` gains `plan_acl` and `hook` discriminators (additive; `kind` is unvalidated).
- **P0.3 Annotation source of truth.** Annotate built-in `fs`/`shell` tools with MCP
  `ToolAnnotations` (`readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint`/`idempotentHint`/`openWorldHint`) at their
  definition sites; `is_read_only` and the ACL matcher consume annotations uniformly for built-ins

## Pillar 1 — Planning mode (rebuilt on the engine)

### P1.0 Skill privileged-effects substrate (owner-requested foundation)
Skills today return **text** with no side effects (`skill_runtime.py:213-315`). Add a **declared,
runtime-executed privileged-effect** capability to the skill contract — a structured effect the
runtime performs on invocation (never via returned text, so it's injection-safe). Two effects:
- **`enter_mode`** — transition the session mode (plan-entry rides this).
- **`spawn_subagent_with_skill`** — run the skill in a fresh subagent instead of inlining it into
  the current context (parity with Claude Code / Codex skill-as-subagent).

This generalizes cleanly to future variants (`plan_workflow`, `plan_small` — same substrate, more
thinking room). Ties into the skill-semantics and agents-creating-agents campaigns. The `planning`
skill is the first `enter_mode` consumer.

### P1.1 MODE — declarative ACL, not copy-pasted Python
Delete the 3× hardcoded lock; re-express as priority-banded `plan_acl` rows on P0:
```
deny  *                              @40  modes=[plan]     # deny everything
allow *  annotations.readOnly=true   @50  modes=[plan]     # re-allow read-only by capability
allow  ask_user, web_fetch, plan_exit @50 modes=[plan]
deny   <write/edit tools>            @65  modes=[plan]     # classifiable file tools: hard-denied
allow  <write/edit>  path=<plans>/*.md @70 modes=[plan]    # the sole writable path
```

  bash-parser trap; #1032 deleted that heuristic and ⚑#3 forbids it): plan-mode shell runs under

  `npm test`→`target/` succeeds, `prettier --write` fails `EROFS`, `git commit` fails — the Codex

  (advisory) not a hard block (`sandbox_roots.py:100-102`); file-edit *tools* are hard-denied on
  **all** platforms (classifiable via annotations), only shell-command writes are floor-on-Windows.

- **Plan mode overrides user allow-rules** (priority band, not code-order accident). Subagents
  inherit structurally. `is_read_only` stays the structural first-branch (reads never gated).
- **Delete `chat` mode** (unenforced; duplicates `edit`).

  with P2.2 to keep baseline green).
- **P2.2 Internal middleware interface + subprocess adapter (atomic with the runtime/hooks.py
  port).** One onion interface `wrap(request, next)` over the `ToolRuntimeHooks` seam (call `next`

  envelope with `schema_version`, `hook_id`, session/turn/tool context, `tool_annotations`; stdout
  tagged-union; exit 2 + stderr = deny-with-reason). HTTP + `prompt` (model call) adapters on the
  same interface. Scope-aware discovery (salvaged). Port the four live consumers here.
- **P2.3 Connect `tool_interceptor` + the tool/lifecycle event set.** Wire a hook's tagged-union
  return (`allow`/`deny`/`ask`/`modify`/`synthesize`) into the already-plumbed `tool_interceptor`

  `PostToolBatch` + `SessionStart`/`SessionEnd` + `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop` + `Stop` +
  `PreCompact`. Every event ships `schema_version` + `tool_annotations`.
- **P2.4 BeforeModel/AfterModel via a `dspy.LM` wrapper.** *Not* the turn-level
  `streaming.py`/`turn_forward.py` seam (fires once per turn). A custom `dspy.LM` injected via
  `dspy.context(lm=...)` gives **per-request** granularity: `synthesize`→return a canned completion

  redact→rewrite the outgoing request.
- **P2.5 Invariants (fix in shipped code).** Stable **`id`** (not positional). **Hook failure ≠
  user rejection** (distinct error type/message/telemetry — stop dropping the reason at the
  `pre_tool` boundary). **Tighten-only** (a hook `allow` never overrides a `deny`; fix the ordering
  so `is_read_only` runs *before* any hook — reads stay ungateable). **Most-restrictive-wins** (rides

  deferred loop's checkpoint IS its recorded trajectory, and resume = deterministic replay up to the

  offline-replay machinery we already build. **Nothing here is postponed to a later spike** — the

    once-only (`resolve_permission` is idempotent + the event fires once). The **thread-occupancy

## Decisions (resolved with owner)

- ONE combined campaign, P0 → P1 → P2, live-gated per slice-group. ✔
- Hooks: **delete BOTH** systems; rebuild one on the `ToolRuntimeHooks` seam + subprocess/HTTP/
  in-process/prompt adapters; salvage ideas, not code. ✔ (Q1a)
- Durable defer: YES for **all** yield points — plan_exit + Stop/UserPromptSubmit on the #1031
  substrate, and **PreToolUse** via the generalized parked-gate; **cross-restart** durability rides
  the replay substrate (P2.3/P2.4). Nothing punted to a spike (owner: we defer nothing). ✔ (Q2)
- Synthesize: EVERYTHING now — tool-layer `tool_interceptor` **and** BeforeModel/AfterModel via a
  `dspy.LM` wrapper (per-request synthesize + model routing). ✔ (Q3)
- Plan entry: **skill privileged-effects substrate** (`enter_mode` + `spawn_subagent_with_skill`);
  the `planning` skill is the first `enter_mode` consumer; user toggle too. ✔ (Q4/Q1-followup)
- Plan-mode shell: **OS write-fence, not a parser**; hard on Linux, recorded-floor on Windows;
  file-edit tools hard-denied on all platforms. ✔ (Q2-followup)
- Engine merge fenced to tool+domain+plan_acl+hook; `fs_root` fence stays separate. Delete `chat`
  mode. Epistemic ledger in the plan artifact. No fifth store (state → session record +
  `session.metadata`, the #948 AgentTask pattern — NOT `workflow_state`; audit → semantic
  highway). ✔
- **P4 goal eval: LLM-judge only; loop bounds are the hard stops** (A4 #1057, review-findings
  fix). The initial two-tier design (LLM first-pass + deterministic `StatePredicate`/file hard
  gate over `workflow_state`) was DELETED. The cross-industry survey settled it: nobody ships a
  predicate over model-authored state as the halt authority, and clio's `workflow_state` is
  written by the acting model — so the predicate let it *mark its own homework* (`goal.py:251`
  self-satisfy). The bounded LLM judge is now the sole completion decision; `goal_status` returns
  armed state only (never runs the judge); a judge-met goal stops any armed loop via the
  `turn_finalize` glue (`loop_goal_met`). Accepted residual: the judge is transcript-persuadable,

**Executor:** Codex. **Reviewer:** Claude (this repo's review session). **Flowcept:** owned by a separate session; the owner coordinates its develop merge directly.

## Context

Codex produced four branches (clio-agent `codex/gact-a2ui-v091-producer` @ fc4ea160, gact-tui `codex/gact-tui-node-revamp` @ 2a425f12, marketplace `codex/earthscope-inherit-session-model` @ 8c0e4a2, clio-kit `codex/mcp-launcher-nonblocking-budget` @ d301bf7). An eight-agent review (compliance + five design angles) reached this verdict: **genuinely good architecture, ungoverned** — zero CI ever ran, both large branches fail their own gates, several claims are false at HEAD, and the recurring defect signature is "correct pattern applied once, not carried to the sibling."

Separately, `feat/flowcept-provenance` (14 commits, live-qualified, Flowcept/CMF provenance + blueprint-MCP fixes) was never merged and the Codex rework never saw it. Both branches rewrote the **same blueprint-discovery method** in `agent.py`; git auto-merges them into code neither branch ever ran.

Stop at develop; no release cut.

This session (Claude) reviews the PRs; the other Claude session owns flowcept and lands it first.

## How this campaign runs

This document is the campaign's source of truth. Codex's first act is Phase 0: file the GitHub issue set (one umbrella per repo + one issue per workstream, each carrying its full spec — file:line, failure scenario, acceptance — copied from this doc; issues are the loop's grounding, never bare bodies) and open the four draft PRs so CI becomes the verification loop. Phase 0 umbrellas: clio-agent [#1249](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-agent/issues/1249), gact-tui [#371](https://github.com/iowarp/gact-tui/issues/371), marketplace [#54](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-agent-marketplace/issues/54), clio-kit [#381](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-kit/issues/381).

**All owner decisions are resolved in this document — there are none left to ask mid-campaign.** (See the final section.)

## Non-negotiable ground rules (violations reopen the PR)

1. **No silent fallback** — every degradation emits a typed reason reaching trace/API (model: `_stream_fallback_reasons` in `gact/streaming.py`). No bare `except: pass`, no `contextlib.suppress(Exception)` on new paths.
2. **No ratchet raises** — `check_file_size.py` / `check_silent_fallbacks.py` baselines go DOWN only. Fix accretion by moving code into owner modules, never by editing baselines.
3. **Tests first for bugfixes** — every bug below lands with a failing-first test; error paths and concurrency, not just happy path.
4. **Server owns semantics** — no new client-side filters/heuristics; deleting one means filing+fixing the server defect it masked.
5. **Two-lane observability** — model lane bounded (lean), trace/UI lane byte-verbatim; **no trace-lane fact may be derived from a model-lane projection**.
6. **Protocol by negotiation, never timing** — no global timeouts over composite work; version/era from handshake only.
7. Do not touch `.tmp/clio-agent-flowcept` (another session's worktree). Conventional commits, no `--no-verify`.

## Phase 0 — Freeze, open draft PRs, file the issue set

1. Stop feature work on all four branches (done — tips above are final inputs).
2. **Open draft PRs immediately** for all four branches against their targets (clio-agent→develop, gact-tui→develop, marketplace→main, clio-kit→main). CI only triggers on PRs/develop/main — this is the verification loop for everything below. Record the red baseline of the first runs.
3. File GitHub issues from this plan: one umbrella per repo + one issue per workstream below, **with the full spec (file:line, failure scenario, acceptance) copied in** — never bare issue bodies. Link all to the umbrella.

## 1. Ground rules

1. **Grounding release first.** A release is cut from the current state before any of this executes,
   so every change diffs against a known-good shipped baseline.
2. **Branches map to issues.** Every change lands on a branch named for its issue; no work stranded
   in local-only commits. One behavior change per PR.
3. **Spec follows reality.** The GACT contract (`gact-tui/contract/SPEC.md`) drifted because it was
   never updated while the implementation evolved. Convergence direction: **re-reconcile the spec to
   today's implementation** (reality leads, spec documents, conformance enforces) — do NOT regress
   code to the stale documented contract. Exception: where the implementation is self-contradictory
   (the `message.created` nesting fork, inconsistent error tags, capability flags that lie), pick the
   coherent current behavior and codify it. See gact-tui [#232](https://github.com/iowarp/gact-tui/issues/232).
4. **Every degraded path is loud.** Silent `try/except → fallback` is a defect class, not a style
   choice. House style to copy: the typed `stream_fallback` reason catalog (`gact/streaming.py`).
   See [#772](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-agent/issues/772).
5. **Every bugfix lands with a failing-first regression test.** Depth over breadth: wrong inputs,
   error paths, concurrency. See [#773](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-agent/issues/773).
6. **Delete, don't gate.** Dead layers and banned heuristics are removed, not env-flagged off.
7. **No accretion.** Patch-driven development is how `turn.py`/`agent.py`/`app.py` grew to 3–4k
   lines; cleanup work must not feed them. A fix that adds more than a trivial amount of code goes
   in an owner module (new file if needed), not appended to a god file. Now that the #767
   split has landed, CI carries **enforcing** guards (`scripts/check_file_size.py`,
   `scripts/check_no_class_in_function.py`) that hold each god-file at a per-file ratchet
   baseline (may only ratchet down) and fail any new offender, so files can't silently regrow (#774).

## 3. Systemic diagnoses

Full evidence lives in the issue bodies; one line each here.

1. **Nothing was ever deleted.** Two turn engines (`agent.py` loop + `gact/turn.py`); `agent.py`'s
   Tier-2 arm is scaffolding around a hard-failing stub; three console entrypoints; dead registry/
   optimizer/ARC-cache halves; a doctor probing a deployment shape that no longer exists.
2. **The same job implemented N times.** 9 final-answer paths · 4 routing-decision types ·
   7 persistence locations · 3 DSPy field-marker parsers · 2 event vocabularies double-published
   per token (one with zero consumers) · 2 agent-resolution pipelines that already disagree ·
   2 history injections per turn · 2 LSM instances on the same files.
3. **One protocol, four hand-copied type systems.** Python/Go/TS + per-adapter vocabularies, no
   codegen; every checked enum drifted in the hand-copied layers; server AND clients both own text
   dedup — live≠reload by construction.
4. **Banned deterministic heuristics still run.** Keyword guards veto/replace model answers in
   `agent.py`; EarthScope demo vocabulary baked into "generic" core (merge/delegation/evidence) and
   into the TUI's placeholder strings; personal SSH registry URL + demo agent as product defaults.
5. **Config & repo entropy.** 89 env vars (37 via `conf`, 50 undocumented, 13 phantom-documented);
   runtime rebind mutates `os.environ` and blocks the migration; meta-docs (CLAUDE.md/PLAN.md)
   actively miscalibrate agent sessions; 669 MB media pack in gact-tui; junk at both roots.
6. **TUI streaming parity gap** (owner-reported, confirmed): the web/gact streaming + thinking-trace
   rework was never ported to the TUI — dual projection, unconsumed normalized channel, half-matched
   semantic allow-list.
7. **Silent failover semantics** (owner-reported, confirmed): unlogged `except → fallback` paths
   hide failures throughout both repos.
8. **Test depth** (owner-reported, confirmed): 2,076 tests collect clean but are happy-path biased —
   every audit P0 lives in an error/concurrency/wrong-input path no test exercises.
