## Ownership and lifetime

The existing `AgentTaskRegistry`, `TaskRecordStore` and storage
`TransferOperation` remain authoritative. Shared controls project those owners;
the application supervisor retains drivers, submission RPCs and transports on
the existing application loop. It is not another execution registry.

MCP identities include server, CLIO conversation, backend session and task ID.
After the backend accepts, the existing extension persists the handle before
returning a model-visible receipt. A stopped turn cannot cancel an already-sent
task-capable submission RPC or close its transport before custody recording.
Submission health limits remain. A failed submission never returns acceptance;
uncertain requests are not replayed. Existing orphan persistence errors retain
the backend identity and best-effort cancellation outcome.

The supervisor tracks outstanding acceptance RPCs against their complete
conversation owner. Subtree cancellation closes admission under the same lock
and waits for already-dispatched acceptances to finish recording and enter their
owner's cancellation path. A parent cannot publish cancellation while an
uncertain descendant submission is still settling. Stop only releases the turn's
waiter; it does not close task admission or cancel accepted work.

Relay subagents persist their complete backend key in the existing child-session
metadata before returning a fresh opaque handle. Timeline and lifecycle frames
validate the retained backend key and project onto that handle. Bare backend IDs
remain aliases only when unique; colliding IDs cannot hide another owner or
select the wrong transport after reconstruction.

Accepted MCP drivers reuse exclusive leases, task progress, input-answer
persistence and result collection. HTTP recovery uses the original backend
session and resumes observation without calling the original tool again.
Nonrecoverable lost work is interrupted. A disconnected recoverable task keeps
its backend state separate from connection freshness.

Downloads use the existing approved transfer path with its provider identities,
selected paths, revisions, hashes and cleanup-before-terminal publication.
Indexing persists an operation before enumerating off-loop, deduplicates
equivalent active requests, checks cancellation while traversing and commits
the complete manifest/source pointer/operation in one transaction. Failure,
cancellation or interruption leaves the previous manifest intact. Failure to
record shared custody prevents a newly queued storage worker from starting.

`shell_bash(background=true)` uses the existing confinement and output limits.
The default stays foreground. The owner retains a Windows Job or POSIX process
group, incremental output and explicit execution timeout. Service shutdown
settles owned process trees and records interruption. Recovery never uses a PID
alone to reattach or automatically repeats a command.

## Completion delivery

Terminal results are persisted before completion intent and an in-memory wake.
Existing subagent inbox/enrichment machinery carries every task kind. A busy
conversation receives bounded batches at a safe model boundary. An idle
conversation starts a system-event turn through the existing turn runner,
including after Stop, without another human message. A paused future human
message queue remains paused independently of these task-result turns.

Staging does not consume results. Consumption happens at the existing
commit-to-run boundary after veto checks. Aborted/vetoed turns retain results,
overflow remains queued, and collection between staging and commit cannot
cause duplicate automatic delivery. Submission, progress and result use the
same invocation and handle. Supervisor polling does not fabricate tool calls.

The existing Observability context frame is refreshed at commitment with the
exact surviving task injections. Collection between staging and commitment
must remove the staged text from both model input and its recorded context
frame, while preserving unrelated context and the frame identity.

The task dock, Observability and Runs use the same cancellation operation as
agent controls. An active cancellable task has a confirmation control naming
the assignment; subagent confirmation warns about descendants. Acknowledged
cancellation displays "Cancellation requested" until owner settlement. Dismissal
only hides a row.

The shared REST projection is `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/async-tasks`; cancellation
is `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/async-tasks/cancel`, and explicit result readback is
`GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/async-tasks/{handle}/result`. The existing `/tasks` routes
retain the conversation to-do contract. Dismissed task records remain readable
through shared controls and result readback, while UI listings hide their cards.

## Compatibility

Newly generated default tool catalogs expose shared task controls rather than
agent-only wait/observe/cancel controls. Explicit legacy agent control aliases
delegate to the shared implementation for the first released compatibility
cycle containing this feature. Remove those aliases in the following release,
with migration notes and updated tool declarations. Subagent messaging and
restart are retained. App-less legacy MCP callers retain their existing
transparent result behavior; all supported product bridges require the shared
agent-facing contract.

Compatibility observation keeps the old numeric cursor, bounded curated rows,
workflow-state snapshot and declared structured response while using the shared
wait/Stop/authorization machinery. Grouped collection follows recorded terminal
order on both result and event lanes. Shared result collection uses the existing
model-result bound and session-owned spill references, including the complete
stored subagent output; it does not refer to an omitted compatibility tool.

Status: candidate implementation and qualification in progress, 2026-10-11.
The original source audit used core
`8feb486cb84a3c4587d9c424b69861e93925933b` on
`codex/agent-facing-async-tasks`. The branch now includes local lifecycle and
exact-session messaging controls. Live acceptance remains a separate gate.

## Candidate implementation

- `pause_agent(target)`, `resume_agent(target)` and `restart_agent(target, fresh=False)`
  use the existing Subagent registry and original placement owner. Pause persists
  an execution hold before stopping its model; resume keeps the handle. Running
  held runs reserve their admission slot; held queued runs cannot be admitted.
- `cancel_tasks` remains generic across all task kinds. A Subagent cancellation
  closes admission and settles its descendant owners before publishing completion.
- `message_agent(target=..., message=..., scope=..., user_intent=..., wake=False,
  reply_to=..., correlation_id=...)` accepts exact session IDs or task handles.
  The old `task_id` argument remains an alias. Sender-attributed mail is durable
  before acknowledgement and is collected at model iteration boundaries or an
  automatic idle wake. A hold prevents both paths from consuming pending results.
- A terminal recipient creates a linked successor without reparenting. Full
  retained messages have new IDs and references to their original message IDs;
  fresh mode omits history. Current parent restrictions compose with retained
  recipient policy. Restart retries against one old handle reuse its successor.
- A retained successor may read a known terminal task result from its own prior
  run lineage with `get_task_result`. Registry links, recipient identity and
  workspace must agree. This does not enumerate historical tasks, grant task
  control, expose live work or consume the predecessor's completion mailbox.
  Fresh-context runs, deleted sources and unrelated peer sessions retain their
  ordinary result scope.
- Memory search and summary results include exact message targets after read-scope
  checks. Peer messaging additionally requires scoped intent; discovery does not
  grant pause, resume, restart or cancellation authority.
- The HTTP doors are `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/agent-controls/{target}/{action}`
  and `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/agent-messages`. UI and native tools call the same
  lifecycle and messaging owners. Task surfaces expose pause requested, paused,
  resume and confirmed restart separately from cancellation.
- Local holds cannot pause a remote model. Relay pause/retained-context restart
  and peer relay addressing are explicitly refused until the remote protocol
  supports their contract; existing owner-to-relay messaging is retained. Those
  routes remain unimplemented and unqualified, not silently simulated locally.

## Restart custody across successor chains

Every linked restart carries a bounded, validated briefing of accepted operation
identities and prior-run outcomes from the existing registry/session lineage.
This applies to retained and fresh context modes. The original assignment,
operation handles, provider/backend-session identities and prior messages remain
unchanged. Private workflow state and unbounded result content are excluded.
Missing/cyclic/conflicting lineage, ambiguous handles or oversized custody reject
the new launch rather than silently dropping accepted work. Validation precedes
the idempotency shortcut; a returned successor must retain the same owner, agent,
workspace and placement. Valid retries reuse the already accepted successor.

An empty current-scope task query does not mean no earlier operation was accepted.
The successor uses its explicit historical briefing to avoid replay. That
briefing grants no historical query, control or live-result access; fresh-context
result restrictions and existing retained terminal-result authorization remain.

The fresh-context briefing quotes the original assignment as historical data and
places the current restart instructions afterward. Fresh resets the copied
transcript, not accepted-operation custody. Historical launch instructions do
not request another execution of already accepted work. Explicit new messages
remain separate and retain their sender authority. This guidance addresses an
actual Codex replay on `abe59c8e`; wording alone is not a deterministic execution
deduplication mechanism. The affected model lifecycle gates require rechecking.

## Human intervention and ownership

Human control never silently changes an agent's owned work. Authorized human
steering, pause, resume, cancellation, restart and child-session Stop are relayed
to the **actual immediate owner**, independently of which ancestor's UI issued
the command. A nested Shell or Download notifies its owning child; controlling
that child notifies its parent. Subagent cancellation/restart notices explicitly
identify the descendant cascade. Dismissal remains a display operation.

Notices use the existing durable agent mailbox and its regular next-model-call
boundary, idle wake, hold, batching and commit-to-run rules. They carry human
attribution, action, original handle, kind, assignment, target session, status
before the action and recorded outcome. A restart outcome includes the new handle
and predecessor link. A human request is saved before control execution; an
uncollected request is updated with its acknowledgement/error. If the model has
already received a long-running request, its outcome is queued as a linked
follow-up. Requested cancellation is never presented as physical settlement.

Both current and compatibility HTTP controls are covered, along with accepted
user feedback sent directly to a child, queued-message promotion and human Stop
from HTTP/A2UI. Replayed accepted messages retain one notification identity.
Agent-initiated controls continue to return their ordinary tool observations;
they do not impersonate a human intervention. Target authorization remains ahead
of relay, and a notice neither transfers permissions nor instructs the parent
to automatically undo a human control or replay accepted work.

| Cross-session messaging | The tool takes a task ID, not a session ID from memory search. The shared messaging helper looks up the application-wide task registry without the caller-session authorization used by shared task controls. ## Pause, Stop, cancel and restart

These meanings are distinct. The agreed default for Pause is a durable hold
until explicit resume or an explicitly waking owner message.

| Action | Agent execution | Accepted descendant tasks | Identity and notifications |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Conversation Stop | Stops the current model turn and its waiter. | Continue. | Existing task completion can automatically wake the agent. |
| Pause subagent | Stops model execution cooperatively and holds future automatic model starts. | Continue; progress and results remain durable. | Same Subagent handle/session; nonterminal `paused` effective status. No completion notification for merely pausing. |
| Resume subagent | Clears the hold and continues using retained context and pending messages/results. | Continue. | Same handle/session; resumes once at an eligible boundary. |
| Cancel subagent | Ends this run and closes its subtree admission. | Explicit cancellation cascades through descendants, with cleanup before settlement. | Original handle settles `cancelled`; does not become active again. |
| Restart subagent | Starts a new linked run after the prior run has settled. | Never automatically replays or duplicates accepted operations. | New handle; old result/history immutable. Default context continuation, with an explicitly requested fresh mode. |

Pause is neither OS process suspension nor a promise that an ordinary foreground
RPC stops immediately. It must report `pause_requested` until the provider/turn
owner has stopped reaching further model/tool boundaries. Execution safeguards
for in-flight foreground work remain intact. Accepted background tasks must not
inherit the pause signal as task cancellation.

A paused Subagent remains active for queries and mixed waits. An unbounded wait
can remain pending until resume or cancellation. Its displayed supported actions
include resume, message, observe and cancel; generic MCP/Download/Indexing/Shell
tasks do not acquire subagent pause or restart semantics.

Restart defaults to continuing the retained assignment/context, rather than
blindly running the initial assignment again. The new run must know which work
already completed, failed or remains accepted. A fresh restart is an explicit
mode that preserves old evidence and still does not replay accepted operations
implicitly. If restart is requested while running, first settle the old run;
never allow overlapping replacements or reopen a cancelled subtree in place.

## Proposed model-facing controls

Keep shared `query_tasks`, `observe_tasks`, `wait_tasks`, `cancel_tasks` and
`get_task_result`. Add subagent-specific `pause_agent`, `resume_agent` and
`restart_agent`. Extend the existing `message_agent` instead of creating a second
message transport.

Targets must be explicit and unambiguous: a task handle for one run, or a session
ID for one conversation. Preserve the old `task_id` argument as a compatibility
alias. A session target resolves its current eligible run, or explicitly creates
a linked continuation when the previous run is terminal. An expert ID such as
`ndp` alone is insufficient because several instances may exist.

`message_agent` returns a durable message acknowledgement immediately, including
message ID, source/target sessions, target run handle, disposition and any
successor relation. Busy recipients see it before their next model iteration;
idle recipients wake without another human message. Paused recipients can receive
and retain messages; a declared `wake` option decides whether the message resumes
them. Terminal recipients create a linked continuation, including after failure
or cancellation, rather than modifying the old terminal result.

Messages retain sender identity and provenance. Peer-agent messages are agent
content, not human instructions or parent-authoritative steer. Preserve the
recipient's agent definition, workspace, model policy and permissions. Delivery
must not transfer the sender's capabilities or silently reparent the recipient.
Replies need explicit reply/correlation IDs; do not create an unconditional
automatic reply loop. Task completion continues to belong to its original owner;
peer messaging does not consume another conversation's completion mailbox.

## Find a session, read context, then address it

The existing memory tools are a useful foundation, but their names hide limits:

| Tool | Actual source and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `memory_search_sessions` | Lexical term matching over retained transcript `text`, `thinking` and `error` parts, ranked by matched-term fraction and recency. Hits carry session/message/part IDs and bounded excerpts. It is not a search over generated session summaries or a semantic ARC index. |
| `memory_read_session_summary` | Generated on demand from session metadata, message counts and up to the last five messages, each excerpt capped at 360 characters. It also returns message IDs and rollback metadata. No summarizer model creates this value; it is not a whole-session narrative. |
| `memory_read_context_frame` | Reads one retained context-assembly record: model/agent identity, referenced messages/files/injections, inclusion decisions and token estimates. It returns up to 50 items. It is not a general reader for the contents of those referenced messages/files. |

`_record_context_frame` creates frames during turn preparation. The audited path
stores them in a bounded `app.state.context_frames` ledger initialized empty at
application startup. No durable frame restore path was found in this audit;
therefore do not promise historical frame availability after restart. Message
and session persistence are separate from this frame ledger.

Sources: `gact/memory_tools.py`, `gact/routes/memory.py`,
`gact/runtime/memory_search.py`, `gact/enrichment.py`, `gact/turn_start_offloop.py`,
`gact/runtime/retention.py` and `gact/app.py` under `src/clio_agent/`.

The current memory policy allows same-session reads, same-workspace reads with
user intent, and separately scoped global-workspace reads. Arbitrary other
workspaces remain denied. Global workspace is not a wildcard over all projects.
Search filters for agent/kind/status/time and cursor pagination are desirable
extensions; the current native search exposes query/scope/limit/user_intent only.

Keep memory retrieval and execution controls distinct. Add live session/run
identity and addressable target information to discovery results after scope
checks. A discovered session does not automatically grant pause/cancel/restart
authority. Owner/descendant controls retain their existing authority; authorized

For deeper reading, follow provenance to bounded message/context ranges with

3. Extend the existing successor path for explicit restart and terminal messaging.

4. Introduce a shared target resolver and messaging policy used by both HTTP and

5. Add matching UI actions and shared model guidance; keep dismissal distinct.

Focused checks must cover pause-versus-completion/message/admission races,

identity, no duplicate and no silent reparenting. Include UI review and all
distinct local/relay/provider routes. Repeat affected lifecycle races five times.

This source audit is not a live model demonstration. Earlier async-task receipts
keep their original source identities and do not qualify these proposed controls.

## 1. Direction and public contract

Replace the accumulated task integration, preserving requirements and useful workload algorithms rather than its module graph. All requested task, subagent, session, peer and workflow capabilities remain in scope. Use codex/agent-facing-async-tasks in core and GACT; record the GACT commit in core. Preserve unrelated work, installed Desktop, authentication, defaults and released pins.

Use two execution families:
- FastMCP Tasks owns ordinary Shell, Download and Indexing execution. External MCP servers own their tasks.
- CLIO's conversation engine owns agent assignments, model execution and lineage. Root and child agents share that implementation. Preserve the existing relay transport's MCP task identity/idempotency and message route as an agent-placement adapter; it may carry an agent assignment but does not create a second CLIO execution lifecycle.

Register product built-ins through FastMCP. Short control tools delegate to the existing owner; they are not themselves background tasks. Built-in task calls use the owning native runtime root. Preserve capability-based direct routing for declared MCP servers so task-capable servers are not sent through a Tasks-suppressing ProxyClient; do not blanket-toggle unrelated client capabilities. Register task tools before their owning server starts. Future Labios support attaches at this MCP boundary, without a speculative scheduler.

Preserve the shared tools:
- query_tasks(kind=None, status=None, handle=None, tool=None, agent=None, active_only=False, cursor=None, limit=50, scope="tree")
- observe_tasks(tasks, cursor=None, pattern=None, timeout_s=None, notify=None)
- wait_tasks(tasks, return_when="all", timeout_s=None)
- cancel_tasks(tasks)
- get_task_result(handle)

Accept one handle or a list. Kinds are Subagent, Session, MCP, Download, Indexing, Shell and Question; transport/placement are separate fields. Queries expose assignment, display label, owner, raw backend status, effective status, activity, progress, timestamps, supported actions and result reference. Preserve the original subagent assignment before launch enrichment. Optional CLIO task-description metadata is removed before backend arguments; derive safe descriptions otherwise and identify missing legacy descriptions.

The user-approved Question extension is an implementation and qualification gate.
ask_user always posts through the existing question owner and returns a durable
handle immediately. It is a short FastMCP control operation, with no execution
worker or separate scheduler. The question owner records full history in Core;
its live UI dictionary is a rebuildable projection. Shared query/observe/wait,
result collection and cancellation use that owner through the same task surface.
wait_tasks(question_handle) explicitly waits for an answer, unbounded by default.
An answer already recorded returns immediately. Stop cancels the waiter and
leaves the question open; cancel_tasks explicitly dismisses the question.
Answers use the recipient-input completion boundary instead of the composer FIFO,
so they can enter the next iteration or wake an idle session without duplicate
automatic delivery. Permission and external MCP input gates retain their own
authorization requirements. Qualify mixed Question/Shell/Subagent waits, busy
and idle answers, Stop independence, recovery and attributed human controls with
actual models before claiming this extension complete.

Authorize before lookup disclosure, filtering, counts and pagination. Default scope is the caller's tree. scope="authorized" permits peer/root discovery only through trusted owner grants; model-supplied intent is not authority. Reuse existing permission policy and explicitly represent missing coordination grants as Core relationships (granting human, recipient session/assignment, target scope, read/observe/message/control rights); only authenticated human actions or trusted configured policy create grants. Reading/messaging does not grant cancellation. Memory session discovery returns stable session addresses and task links subject to the same permissions.

Query and observe do not consume completion. Mixed waits return individual outcomes and pending handles; one failure never cancels other members. Waits are unbounded by default; zero is a snapshot and positive expiry ends only the waiter. Reuse native result driving instead of adding another polling implementation. notify=True subscribes the caller to the exact handle, False removes that subscription, and omission leaves it unchanged. Owner notifications are automatic; peer collection never consumes them.

## 2. Execution, context and recovery

Persist a submission with its opaque public handle, immutable owner/assignment identity, invocation, workspace, permissions, confinement, attribution, tool arguments and explicit execution limits before invoking the backend. Public acceptance follows native acceptance and confirmed persistence of the full backend identity. A confirmed pre-acceptance failure is a submission error. Failure to record identity after native acceptance is accepted-but-recording-unconfirmed; loss of the submission reply is acceptance-uncertain. Return the existing public handle and the distinction, never a clean retryable submission error. Preserve this recovery evidence and never blindly submit again.

For CLIO-owned task tools, carry an opaque submission reference explicitly into the native queued invocation, hidden from the model-facing schema. One shared request boundary validates public arguments, strips/rejects model-supplied internal fields and injects its host-owned reference. Store the reference with the exact tool and argument digest in Core. The actual registered worker callable resolves this trusted context and binds it to its full native task identity under the application-owned writer's serialization before effects; reject a different task using that reference, while recording same-task redelivery as another attempt. In-process authorization comes from this host-owned binding, not an assumed MCP access token. Do not depend on inherited ContextVars or request middleware executing inside Docket. Missing, mismatched or unrecoverable context fails before workload effects. Revalidate current revocations and descendant cancellation admission when execution starts.

Shell retains background=false by default. Both execution modes use the same native workload implementation and retain its native handle internally:
- background=true returns the public handle immediately; Stop or cancelled waits leave it running.
- background=false awaits the result; turn Stop explicitly cancels that native task and awaits its process-tree cleanup. Never rely on transparent call_tool cancellation.
- If Stop races with submission, finish recording acceptance. Apply the appropriate foreground cancellation or background continuation rule without resubmission.

GACT application lifespan owns the native server roots, clients and result observers on its application event loop. They do not live on resident SyncMCPToolExecutor threads and are excluded from that fleet's idle reaper. Provider bridges submit onto this application loop. Remove inherited whole-call deadlines after acceptance; retain submission/RPC health limits and explicit workload execution limits. Their responsibilities are transport retention, observation, input routing and confirmed recording, not workload scheduling. Persist outcomes before creating completion intent. Observers use native driving/status calls to refresh active metadata well within its TTL and promptly store terminal output in Core. Native expiry/not-found means uncertain or expired backend visibility, not proof of failed execution. Known CLIO-owned cancellation may use the authenticated original Docket execution identity if protocol metadata expired; external owners report uncertainty. Native polling creates no extra agent tool calls.

Use embedded memory:// by default. Expose native backend and worker settings through existing configuration; document that local execution does not survive process loss. Shell and a new connected-storage FastMCP server each have an independent native runtime root/lifespan, Docket queue identity and worker pool (configurable concurrency, default 10 each), managed on the application event loop. The shared catalog supplies names, but task calls and controls route through native SDK clients to their owning runtime root; mounting beneath one worker-owning gateway is not pool isolation. These remain MCP calls, never direct Python dispatch. Expose queued versus actually started execution in both background task rows and foreground invocation progress. Do not implement CLIO scheduling or per-tool queues.

Recovery promises honest uncertainty, not exactly-once effects:
- CLIO does not automatically resubmit uncertain accepted operations when an agent or service restarts.
- Native backend recovery/redelivery can repeat or overlap execution after lease loss; report observed attempts and uncertainty honestly. Keep blocking work off the worker event loop. We do not promise globally exclusive execution. A configured persistent backend does not strengthen this guarantee.
- Resume the agent with its assignment, fixed context checkpoint, handles, last confirmed observations and an explicit recovery notice. It can inspect effects, collect results, reconnect existing work, retry unchanged work or submit a revised operation.
- An explicit resubmission gets a new linked handle; old outcomes remain historical. Do not add an exactly-once engine or side-effect rollback promise.
- Reattach surviving external transfers/jobs only using their verified original identity. Never infer custody from a PID alone.
- On shutdown, stop admission, explicitly cancel/withdraw owned active and queued local native executions before leaving their FastMCP lifespans, show pending settlements and record interruption or uncertainty before closing Core. An operator or the implementing agent supervising its own verified qualification processes may force-close unresolved shutdown with recorded uncertainty (or recording unconfirmed during Core outage). Agent-owned qualification processes and disposable data require no further cleanup permission. No hidden automatic cutoff is introduced. Do not mark external surviving work interrupted merely because the local observer stopped. No hidden execution or settlement deadline.

Workload requirements:
- Qualification resource ownership includes the complete descendant process tree and disposable data generated by those processes, even after the original launcher exits. Track and verify creation identities and ancestry; the implementing agent may stop/force-close those owned descendants and remove their disposable data without another permission request.
- Shell keeps confinement, output bounds/references, incremental output, explicit execution limits and process-tree cleanup.
- Downloads reuse approved providers, selected paths/revisions, byte/hash accounting and cleanup-before-terminal. connected_data_download submits the native task; remove the separate transfer scheduler.
- Connect indexing runs as a native task; enumerate off the application loop with progress/cooperative cancellation, deduplicate equivalent active requests within the owning session (provider, revision, paths, indexing options, workspace and permission scope) and atomically publish the complete manifest. Check/reserve deduplication under existing submission serialization before creating another native submission; return the existing handle with reused=true rather than enqueueing a second task or minting a second submission reference. Failure/cancellation/interruption preserves the previous manifest.
- Obtain CLIO-owned workload approvals before execution. Native input_required on external tasks reaches the existing question surface even when the agent is idle, with persisted request/answer identity. Input-answer re-entry and reconnect must not cause CLIO to replay submission.

Preserve cancellation request separately from raw terminal status and physical settlement. Use the shared owner start/cancel admission boundary to distinguish confirmed never started, started with cleanup confirmed, and settlement unknown. A queued cancellation can settle without running a body; prove withdrawal/non-admission rather than awaiting a finally that will never execute. A started invocation's shared server wrapper writes a cleanup receipt after required cleanup. Start observations and receipts identify their execution attempt; an old receipt cannot settle a redelivered attempt. Controls/UI show Cancellation requested while actual settlement remains pending, and expose uncertainty honestly. For external servers, never claim process termination from a cancel acknowledgement alone.

## 3. Assignments, Core history and delivery

A session is a stable address, history and mailbox. An assignment/run is finite delegated or human-started work with one task handle. A model turn is one execution segment; an iteration is one model call and its tool observations. Existing standing watcher assignments retain their handle across check segments, including a failed check; their owner records waiting/error activity, and explicit disarm ends the assignment. They do not publish a completed assignment after each check or wake their parent as a side effect of checking it.

Ordinary yields, task-result wakes, steering, pause/resume and recovery continue the same active assignment. Do not complete its handle merely because the model turn ended. Extend the existing finish/submit boundary with a separate orchestration argument assignment_disposition="yield"|"complete"; it is not a signature output. A direct response without a disposition yields while owned tasks, declared dependencies or input remain pending; otherwise it completes. Explicit completion may leave accepted background work running, and this is recorded. Prompts explain this choice, and the parent/UI can see yielded activity and its pending dependencies. A later message/result after actual completion creates a linked new assignment in the same session and wakes it automatically under the ordinary pause/input/veto gates, as explicitly required; it does not reopen the completed handle or re-enable a stopped goal/loop. Explicit restart also creates a new linked assignment/handle. Subscription and result handles stay pinned to their original assignment; messaging aliases may resolve to the stable session, never silently retarget historical cancellation/results. scope="tree" follows the stable owning session and its delegated descendants, including predecessor assignments. Linked successors in that session retain read/collect/observe/control rights over predecessor-owned work, subject to current revocations; they do not acquire unrelated peer rights. Cancelling a successor includes still-active inherited background work and its delegated descendants, without changing the historical ownership or outcome of old handles.

Pause holds model execution and preserves context; accepted background tasks continue and accumulate results. Resume releases the hold. Cancel applies to every task kind; agent-assignment cancellation closes descendant admission and cancels its task subtree, settling after required cleanup. Restart of an active assignment follows explicit cancellation/settlement; an already terminal assignment can restart directly. Uncertain settlement returns that uncertainty instead of fabricating completion or silently launching a successor.

Keep complete messages, observations, assignments, subscriptions, interventions, lineage and delivery history in Core's existing hierarchy and confirmed writer path. Session metadata contains bounded rebuildable projections, not whole retained histories. There is no new canonical database, execution registry or copied transcript. Restart references a fixed Core history/checkpoint boundary and later accepted-operation observations.

Every stable session owns one Core-backed mailbox. Human feedback, peer messages, attributed runtime notices and task-result references share its recipient-input boundary. A task handle addresses a finite assignment or operation; its notifications target the owning session mailbox, which survives linked assignments and restarts. A workflow groups sessions and grants rather than introducing another delivery queue. Resident projections are rebuildable Core views, not another message inbox. An application-loop signal carries only the session address and requests a fresh Core pending-input check; losing that signal cannot erase accepted content. Startup and busy-to-idle transitions recheck Core. Distributed transports can later deliver the same identities and attributed content through this acceptance boundary without changing acknowledgement or authorization.

Accepted input keeps its original assignment binding. Replay verifies content identity, rechecks admission, and reconciles question answers and parent notices from the confirmed input. It neither dispatches a replacement operation nor retargets a successor. Only recipient-input persistence acknowledges delivery; inspecting or staging a message does not consume it.

Use one authoritative recipient-input commit record in the existing context lane, containing assignment/iteration identity, fixed context boundary and included notification IDs/content references. Write referenced content first, then this confirmed commit; acknowledgements derive from it. put_many is not a transaction. Before the commit, interrupted staging stays pending; after it, recovery reconstructs that input, including the crash window before the model call. Explicit tool-result collection uses the same record after its observation is stored. Delivery is recoverable with stable IDs, not exactly-once external model execution.

Use one application-owned Core writer for these lifecycle commits. Normally persist before projections, terminal waiters and notifications. During a Core outage, confirmed control effects and cleanup observations may update provisional UI/control outcomes and local waiters as recording unconfirmed; this exception includes cleanup receipts, not only parent notices. It never acknowledges durable delivery or promises recovery after an application crash. Native execution remains native; Core records observations and delivery evidence, not a competing task state machine. Create subscriber notifications from durable terminal observations and indexed recipient relationships, without per-subscription workers or whole-session scans.

Keep all mailbox history. gact.mailbox.max_pending_messages defaults to 0/unset, meaning unlimited. A positive setting counts only undelivered messages, including staged messages until input commit. Apply retryable backpressure to new peer-message admission; already-accepted results, ordinary human feedback and human-control records remain durable and cannot be blocked or dropped by that limit. Resident/context batch bounds are not retention limits.

Human steering/pause/resume/cancel/restart records intent in the controlled owner, independent of mailbox capacity, then applies control and derives an attributed parent notice. If Core is unavailable or intent persistence fails, trusted cancellation/pausing of known active work still proceeds through its existing owner using verified identity; report recording as unconfirmed and reconcile its notice when Core returns. Retain pending evidence in application memory only, without another canonical store; a crash during that outage cannot promise durable notice recovery. Reject new durable submissions and do not acknowledge undurable messages as accepted. Parent notices enter the same next-iteration injection path. Repeated controls use their request identity without issuing duplicate effects.

## 4. One admission path, UI and replacement map

Consolidate reservation/admission into the existing conversation queue/TurnRunner under the same session serialization as busy-to-idle transitions; the present spawn() is not already an admission gate. Use this one final decision and one per-iteration durable injection boundary. Include user feedback, composer-queue promotion/autostart suspension, task completions, peer messages, goal continuation, loops/schedules, deferred hooks, A2UI actions, spotter requests, lifecycle resume, elicitation/blocking-question answers, plan-exit approval/revision and blueprint revision gates. Replace the composed idle-hook chain's competing admission decisions.

- Busy: inject eligible feedback/results before the next model call; never start a parallel turn.
- Explicitly paused: retain until explicit resume.
- Waiting for human input: preserve the input gate; the matching answer releases it.
- Idle, including after turn Stop or explicit assignment completion: eligible messages/results wake the agent automatically.
- Goal dependency waits retain partial results until the declared any/all condition; human feedback still arrives.
- Goals, schedules and loops retain their independent enabled/disabled policies. A task wake does not reactivate a disabled control or resume a separately paused future-message queue.

Serialize pending-item checks with busy-to-idle transitions. An arrival during shutdown of a turn must either enter its next iteration or trigger subsequent admission. Temporary busy/admission failures recheck on the corresponding state change. Policy vetoes remain visibly pending until that policy changes or explicit human action; do not spin or permanently consume an attempted batch. After application recovery, rebuild pending delivery from Core. Algorithm wakes remain attributed system injections in the owning session.

Extend the Work information surface, Observability and Runs with compact clickable rows: label, kind, status and useful progress first; details/output/history progressively disclosed. Cancellation has an identifying confirmation and descendant warning for agent assignments. Show pending cancellation, disable duplicate requests, and keep dismissal separate. UI and agent tools use the same operations.

Remove, rather than wrap:
- task_shell_owner execution scheduling and storage transfer/indexing schedulers/task_adapter polling;
- custom generic TaskSupervisor execution drivers for ordinary native tasks;
- task_completion_wake policy, mailbox wake policy and attempted-batch maps;
- independent child-forward terminal writes;
- subagent custody/restart/continuation/history reconstruction modules as their behavior moves into the shared conversation lifecycle and Core references;
- mcp_wait_ladder, duplicate completion-consumption guards and loop_inbox's lossy deque, including its payload and hint caches.

Each stable session has one Core-backed mailbox for accepted human feedback,
peer messages, runtime notices and task outcomes. Task outcomes reference their
existing durable result; they do not copy it into another execution registry.
Assignment and task handles identify the work within a session, rather than
creating separate inboxes. Authorization and recipient-specific input commits
apply equally to local and remote producers. Transient TurnRunner signals only
request a Core mailbox check; they carry no message, task result or delivery
state. Lost signals recover from the Core recipient index on startup/readiness.
Restarted assignments keep that stable mailbox address. Human cancellation acts
through the verified execution owner immediately, with its attributed parent
notice entering the same mailbox; it cannot depend on the model reading mail.
Distributed agent hosting additionally needs cross-host turn reservation and
wake transport. The shared mailbox establishes their addressing and durable
input boundary; this local implementation does not qualify distributed hosting.

Retain workload algorithms, process cleanup, native capability/backend identity routing and shipped compatibility aliases. Aliases only delegate. Preserve released completed-child messaging through stable session aliases and linked assignments; historical task results remain unchanged. Migrate records idempotently, including missing descriptions. Drain/settle old owners before cutover. No permanent old-engine fallback. When Core is unavailable, reject new durable background admission explicitly rather than introducing another store or silently calling it durable.

## 5. Construction and completion gates

Build on one integrated feature branch in this order; all capabilities remain required:
1. One complete native Shell slice: trusted worker context, immediate/background versus foreground behavior, acceptance races, physical cancellation, uncertain recovery and durable delivery.
2. Native MCP, Download and Indexing through that proven integration.
3. Shared root/child assignments, lifecycle, Core mailbox/subscriptions and session/workflow coordination.
4. Unified admission with current autonomy behavior, integrated UI and canonical prompts/docs.
5. Final integrated qualification and deletion/cutover checks.

Focused tests run individually/sequentially with one worker. Cover persistence-before-ack, invalid/uncertain submission, authorization/collisions, legacy migration, filters/cursors, mixed controls, input re-entry, queued versus started cancellation, stale attempt receipts, cancellation during Core failure, Stop independence, delivery/collection races, crash before/after input commit, busy-to-idle arrival, veto recovery, overflow/backpressure, more than 1,000 messages and complete retained history. Fill Shell's native worker capacity and prove storage still starts on its independent runtime root.

Real-model gates use production implementations, Codex/Luna by default and Claude where the bridge differs:
- Every kind returns a handle while running and the model performs other work.
- Query/observe, any/all waits, expired waits with continuing work, partial failures, idle completion and exactly-once receipt under ordinary operation.
- Child yield/download/wake/analysis retains one assignment handle; explicit completion and restart follow their distinct rules.
- Stop versus pause versus cancellation; UI human controls notify the parent; actual descendant/process settlement.
- Independent sessions and distinct workflows exercise discovery, messaging, subscriptions, observation/waits and permission denial.
- Real bytes/hashes, indexing manifests/counts, shell output and child output.
- Worker loss after a visible side effect but before result commit; native backend recovery/redelivery uncertainty, agent inspection and explicit revised retry.
- Input/permission handling, transport reconnect and isolated service interruption. Recoverable external jobs remain distinct from interrupted local work.
- Real-service desktop and phone UI review; repeat affected lifecycle race scenarios five times on the final candidate.

Run scoped formatting/lint/types/guards and required CI without weakening assertions/budgets. Every unavailable, failed or skipped required gate remains incomplete. Old evidence supports regression design but is not acceptance of the replacement.

Update canonical prompts for every capable root/child agent, task-capable tool parameter descriptions, and website walkthroughs with real screenshots. Explain yield/completion, automatic idle wakes, foreground/background cancellation and uncertain recovery.

Record processes, ports, generated data and cleanup ownership before qualification launches; settle and remove disposable state after each family. Preserve canonical product history and existing prohibited/manual-only boundaries. Merge, release and installation remain separate actions.

Required CI/checks and acceptance must pass; skipped/unavailable required gates block completion.

Finite live families:
| ID | Runtime/bridge | Completion condition and retained evidence |
| Q1 | Codex/Luna, all seven kinds | handle exists before completion and model does independent work; Question=input_required; Session accepted before inference; optional inline MCP valid inline result |
| Q2 | Codex/Luna, mixed kinds | progress/cursors, observe/pattern, any/all/expired waits, honest failures/uncertainty and continuing pending members |

Include >1,000 retained messages, pending-only/staged backpressure, bounded hot-read work and legacy missing descriptions.

Repeat these six races five times each on the final candidate: R1 Stop/acceptance; R2 late-start/cancel; R3 busy-to-idle arrival; R4 collection/automatic delivery; R5 recipient-input commit recovery; R6 subtree cancellation/admission. Record a matrix row per repeat. Also explicitly gate migration idempotence and uncertainty-then-final delivery.

They are diagnostics, never product deadlines. On expiry mark failed/blocked with current evidence, stop the model turn, explicitly cancel owned work and await settlement. Provider capacity/auth/prerequisite failures are blocked gates, not reasons to patch task code. Freeze scope; a new authority/driver need returns to architecture review.

Publication is a separate gated stage after candidate review. Resolve next version/channel, branch direction and tags using the repository release procedure before publishing; preserve the reviewed GACT/core pair. # Provider continuation clarification after initial implementation review

After confirmed loss of a local native runtime, recovery may create a host-only native continuation for a verified existing provider job. The continuation retains the public task and original custody, records a new local execution identity, and cannot submit provider work. Its acceptance follows the ordinary uncertainty rules; unresolved local publication or cleanup remains uncertain. This clarification does not permit replay of an uncertain original download or introduce a transfer scheduler.

Astra reviewed this narrow clarification read-only after finding the absent provider reattachment path in the initial implementation. Implementation and independent Claude source review remain pending. A saved provider request without a verified job ID is insufficient. A replacement leg requires confirmed loss of the former local worker, current authorization, original provider/source/destination/path custody, and no unresolved earlier continuation. Cancellation permits only provider control and cleanup; publication remains prohibited under cancellation.

## Turn-ending approval owner refinement

Astra's R30 source review endorses using QuestionCommands for UserPromptSubmit
and Stop approvals rather than persisting another permission lifecycle. The
Question captures its exact input revision/content reference, assignment and
context epoch. Permission cards/routes are compatibility projections/delegates;
PreToolUse enforcement, policies and parked-call events keep their existing owner.

Remove the turn-defer permission-row transition, turn-defer metadata mirror,
text-only resume reconstruction and separate resume helpers. A confirmed human
decision releases the same Core input through a verified Question reference;
its typed content/media remain unchanged. Control outcomes stay retained but do
not automatically wake the owner. Explicit Stop denial may stage feedback;
cancellation/expiry cannot approve work or manufacture a continuation.

Veto/setup errors hold only the exact uncommitted attempted input. Other wake
signals cannot retry that input. An authenticated retry binds supersession at
the server acceptance boundary, independently of user-supplied metadata. Early
approval or a changed/withdrawn input makes stale finalization a no-op. Legacy
approvals without exact correlation remain visibly unresolved; no old resolver
fallback is retained. The common Core writer and existing pending recovery path
remain the only persistence/reconciliation infrastructure.

## Input lifetime decisions

- Stop preserves an uncommitted accepted trigger as held. Other accepted eligible pending work, or an explicit resume, allows it to continue in accepted order. An ordinary wake hint alone is not new work. Buffered feedback does not require another Send. This behavior was adjudicated as intentional.
- An explicit trusted retry of that stopped trigger supersedes the exact held revision, as it already does for pre-input hook/execution failures. The original remains in history; it is not delivered alongside its retry.
- Cancelling the assignment withdraws its exact uncommitted admitted trigger and its typed delegation/resume inputs while retaining their history. It does not withdraw unrelated pending messages. An already committed input or a subsequently revised/withdrawn trigger is unchanged.
- Historical ambiguous input ownership is not guessed or automatically replayed.

Persist assignment/turn/input-revision/content correlation in the existing Core mailbox record when an input is admitted. This permits exact cancellation after the reservation has retired, including Stop → cancel and service restart → cancel. It is not inferred from message recency or held reason. Apply trusted retry supersession before ordinary Stop-hold release, including a retry accepted during worker unwind. Explicit resume must handle stopped input rather than returning `already_running`.

Preserve the human's existing submitted-feedback contract: Stop delivers already submitted pending feedback once, in accepted order and with its original IDs, after slot release without requiring another Send. Buffered eligible messages/results are real accepted work; repeated wake hints and health probes are not. Do not introduce a new Stop timestamp rule that silently suppresses accepted feedback or task outcomes. Stop/retry and queued-feedback races must be tested together.

The Runs replacement covers canonical pagination and cross-session listing, all applicable task kinds, stable handles, owner/session navigation and supported controls. Remove unsupported detach/dismiss actions without reinterpreting them as cancellation or history deletion. Retain workflow/provenance navigation; an interrupted workflow tool call cannot determine its accepted children's execution state. Remove special relay requests from settings, infrastructure and navigation as well as Runs. Shared task listing/status decoding must not become another UI lifecycle owner.

The reservation callback retains execution resources and exact source correlation only; it adds no execution registry, task state machine, scheduler or delivery acknowledgement. The conversation owner still records assignment decisions. Remove the superseded body-local Stop writer rather than retaining two paths.

## Review observations requiring judgment

Collection's idempotent common notice publication currently closes the terminal-write/publication race before the shared recipient-input acknowledgement. Removing it without another confirmed owner boundary would permit later duplicate automatic delivery. Keep that behavior unless the owner commit path replaces it completely. Query/observe still never acknowledge completion.

Early cursor/message validation and writer-boundary authorization are not interchangeable: invalid requests must not create subscriptions/messages, and grants must be rechecked after asynchronous gaps. Remove redundant work only after confirming those boundaries remain covered. Do not introduce a new generic state object or coordinator solely to reduce line count; canonical history and passive projections retain their existing owner.

## Construction and acceptance

Finish this Core/GACT correction pass before executing behavior tests. Build regressions together for early/finalizing Stop, Stop/retry, cancel withdrawal, applied-completion gate recovery, pause/resume/cancel, unsubscribed peer media, failed-input-commit media recovery, principal separation and bounded admission work. Preserve current assertions and budgets.

Use the prepared D: repository/environment. All bootstrap, cache, native Core and per-run test state stays inside it; register and settle its processes and data. Do not retry any rejected C: cleanup or touch manual-only processes. No Core/product qualification runs from the C: checkout.

The pytest launcher is `uv run --frozen --no-sync python -B scripts/run_tests.py <case> -n 0`. It establishes the suite's existing owned run directory before pytest plugins load. Direct pytest also establishes isolation at the start of conftest, before application/dependency imports. Temp, application state, user/config/data directories and dependency caches resolve under `<checkout>/.pytest-runtime/run-.../`; escaping runtime-root overrides are rejected. CI uses the launcher without changing its shard, coverage or worker flags. The task model harness likewise rejects proof/state outside its repository and redirects child temp/state paths. These source changes have not been exercised; initial Core/GACT implementation still precedes behavior execution.

Renew both reviews against the resulting committed Core/GACT pair. The next Fable snapshot must include the marketplace's actual root-level agent directories and relevant CI configuration; R31's selection omitted those marketplace files. Preserve bounded source identity receipts and clean the review copy/processes. Then run focused cases sequentially, the SDK lifecycle retry, F03 measurements, required CI and the complete fresh Q1–Q9/R1–R6 matrix. No release, installation or completion claim precedes those gates.

The test isolation changes are committed at `c6ff3b8c` and `72e7993a`. The prepared D: execution checkout has those changes; no pytest or native Core service has launched. Suite cleanup now authenticates the recorded daemon birth time and confirms retirement rather than signalling a PID alone. Unknown ownership/settlement fails cleanup instead of deleting its state.
